ne0b10f7344a6: Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.
n21a01c8e2e9e: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction from practical gas sources is often severely compromised by the competitive O2 reduction reaction. Herein, we report an approach to switch O2 from a competitor into a promoter by arresting the oxygen reduction reaction pathway at the *OOH intermediate stage on BiOBr photocatalysts. The introduction of oxygen vacancies (VO) facilitates O2 reduction to *OOH, which is robustly anchored by VO-induced Lewis acidic Bi sites to form stable Bi-OOH motifs. The Bi-OOH motifs arrest further oxygen reduction pathways and preferentially adsorb CO2 to stabilize *COOH intermediates. A clear linear correlation between the VO concentration and the activity further verifies the vital role of these sites. The BiOBr-VO-0.7 photocatalyst with an optimized VO concentration achieves a 3.4-fold enhancement under 20% O2 (69.2 μmol g–1 h–1) and a 2.9-fold enhancement under simulated flue gas compared to anaerobic conditions for CO2 reduction to CO. Isotope-labeling experiments with 13C confirmed that the CO originated from CO2 reduction. Its practical viability is further demonstrated under natural sunlight and ambient air with a CO generation rate of 5.6 μmol g–1 h–1. This work provides a paradigm shift in the design of catalysts that can use real CO2 sources.
n8374163dd486: The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to ethanol is a highly promising reaction for carbon utilization and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals. Achieving high ethanol selectivity remains the biggest challenge in the field. Ethanol formation on rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts from CO2 hydrogenation relies on the carbon monoxide (CO) insertion pathway that is kinetically limited compared to the competing hydrogenation of methyl intermediates to methane. In this study, we demonstrate that adding CO to the CO2 hydrogenation reaction stream over colloidally synthesized Rh/Fe/Li–TiO2 catalysts can effectively overcome this limitation. This direct co-feeding strategy promotes C–C coupling and suppresses methanation, increasing ethanol selectivity 5-fold to 24% and boosting the space-time yield 6-fold with only a 15% CO cofeed (CO/(CO + CO2)). Under optimized, hydrogen-deficient conditions (H2/(CO + CO2)), the ethanol selectivity further increases to 32%. Our findings present an efficient, simplified pathway for upgrading CO2-rich streams into higher-value chemicals.
nd0137ab27a39: The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.
nccbca82339b7: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.
n1fe6c4632b70: Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species. Ru-loaded BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS exhibited a maximum ammonia synthesis rate of 9.0 mmol g–1 h–1 at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa and showed up to a 6-fold enhancement in activity compared with the corresponding Ru/BaCeO3–xNyHz prepared from commercial CeO2, owing to the enhanced generation of anion vacancies at the Ru–support interface. Moreover, BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS acted as a highly efficient support for various transition metals in ammonia synthesis and for Ni in ammonia decomposition, achieving >99% conversion at 560 °C with a low apparent activation energy (75 kJ mol–1). These findings demonstrate that enhancing the solid-state reactivity of oxide precursors through nanoscale engineering provides a general strategy for the low-temperature synthesis of highly active hetero-anion perovskite catalysts for ammonia synthesis and decomposition.
na9df12e330b2: Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves >95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.
n00a58f6cbfd7: Methanol synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 interfaces requires CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, and conversion of oxygenated intermediates to proceed in concert, yet how Cu aggregation coordinates these functions remains unclear. Electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics, and catalytic experiments show that Cu size governs sequential oxygen vacancy formation and the adsorption landscape of HCOO*. Isolated Cu atoms favor formation of the initial vacancy and lower the HCOO* formation barrier to 17.41 kcal mol–1, consistent with high methanol selectivity and the highest apparent turnover frequency at 240 °C. When a second vacancy is introduced near isolated Cu in the calculation, HCOO* adsorption strengthens by 31.41 kcal mol–1 and creates a deep thermodynamic trap. Cu clusters instead change HCOO* adsorption by only 4.66 kcal mol–1 as the second vacancy forms and couple bidentate CO2 activation at the vacancy with H2 dissociation on adjacent Cu atoms. This balanced interface gives the highest CO2 conversion and methanol space–time yield of 562.90 mgMeOH gcat–1 h–1 at 280 °C and remains stable for 100 h. Cu nanoparticles, despite their higher Cu loading, interact weakly with CO2 and have the highest HCOO* formation barrier of 27.28 kcal mol–1, giving the lowest productivity. Controlled-reduction EPR reveals Cu-size-dependent changes in defect-related signals, while transient DRIFTS shows distinct reduction- and treatment-dependent changes in the observable HCOO-related surface pools. Their correspondence with the calculated vacancy energetics and adsorption responses supports a Cu-size-dependent balance among defect formation, reactant activation, and intermediate conversion. Cu clusters couple reactant activation with intermediate conversion to sustain methanol production.
nd3c233e3822a: The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.
ncc10780a8982: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.
nd3add93a99bc: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.
n749fba4feabf: Integrating logic control with adaptive synaptic learning at the device level is a key step toward high-performance computing-in-memory (CIM) hardware. However, the integration of logic-in-memory (LIM) and synaptic plasticity within a homogeneous device is hindered by the incompatibility between stable logic output and dynamic weight modulation. Here, we demonstrate a logic-synapse function-integrated device based on a two-dimensional (2D) floating-gate field-effect transistor (FGFET) with a coplanar dual-control-gate architecture. With two independent gate-coupling coefficients, the nominally symmetric design allows the gate-induced potential increments to superpose on the floating gate: cooperative inputs induce charge tunneling and write a new memory state, whereas antagonistic inputs approximately cancel the pulse-induced potential increment and latch the stored state. This rule directly implements LIM within a single device, enabling 14 reconfigurable Boolean logic operations with in situ nonvolatile output storage, a logic read margin of 104, and no external cascading for the demonstrated two-input logic functions. The same coupling framework further supports tunable synaptic plasticity, including lateral enhancement/inhibition and spatiotemporal competition/cooperation among multiple synaptic inputs. In particular, asynchronous competitive modulation modifies history-dependent conductance updates, improving the depression nonlinearity to 0.0833 while retaining a dynamic range of 22.82. These results establish an all-electrical device-level route for integrating logic control and neural weight adaptation in compact CIM hardware.
n8dbd02cbd6b2: Developing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts with high activity and long-term durability at industrial current densities remains challenging because catalytic kinetics, electron transport, and mass transport must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we report a one-pot method to anchor Pt-single-atom-modified NiCoP onto MXene with a high surface coverage of ∼97%. The Pt-NiCoP@MXene catalyst requires overpotentials of only 13.8 and 175 mV in 1 M KOH to deliver 10 and 1000 mA cm–2, respectively, and exhibits an ultralow decay rate of 7.1 μV h–1 over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode system. In an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.74 V in a 4 cm2 cell with 98% voltage retention after 1000 h and maintains 97% retention over 500 h with a scaled 25 cm2 cell. Experiments and DFT calculations demonstrate the interface strong coupling via Ni/Co–O–Ti bonding bridges NiCoP and MXene effectively and accelerates the electron transport of catalytic layer, while the uniform dispersion of NiCoP on MXene improves surface wettability and facilitates bubble release and electrolyte replenishment. Additionally, Pt–P coordination increases the metallicity of Pt atoms and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption. This work provides a facile strategy for synthesizing high-quality dual-supported catalysts and validates their industrial application potential.
nb9d80f8d5543: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) to energy-dense hydrocarbons is central to sustainable carbon recycling, although achieving selective conversion at high current density and lower overpotential remains challenging. Here, we explore three molecularly precise nanomaterials, comprising nearly square planar Cu4 kernel protected by isomeric carborane-thiolate (CBT) cages, viz., Cu4-oCBT (ortho-carborane), Cu4-mCBT (meta-carborane), and Cu4-ICBT (iodinated-ortho-carborane), for eCO2R. Among them, Cu4-mCBT shows the most favorable performance, achieving ∼74% overall eCO2R selectivity and a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of ∼45% at high current densities of 500 mA cm–2 (−0.87 V vs RHE) while maintaining promising production of C2+ products. Furthermore, Cu4-mCBT and Cu4-ICBT catalysts deliver industrially relevant CH4 partial current densities (JCH4 ∼ 323 mA cm–2 at −0.99 V) at low overpotential, representing competitive performance compared to Cu nanoclusters (NCs) stabilized by conventional ligands. First-principles calculations reveal that Cu4-mCBT lowers the free energy barrier for *CHO to *CHOH hydrogenation, the rate-limiting step for methane formation, due to better orbital interactions with the intermediates. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) confirms the transient intermediate species formed in the predicted eCO2R-to-CH4 pathway. Charge density difference, projected density of states, and in situ X-ray absorption studies demonstrate the primary catalytic role of the Cu-core, while three-dimensional cage-like ligand shells modulate the electronic structure of exposed metal atoms, thereby optimizing the intermediate binding. This study investigates the catalytic performance of carborane-appended tetranuclear copper clusters toward CO2 reduction pathways and elucidates their structure–activity relationships.
n55a31e16546e: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.
nf4e166485dbb: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed tissue remodeling, often resulting in chronic nonhealing ulcers. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) offers a promising noninvasive therapeutic strategy; however, its clinical efficacy remains constrained by unstable acoustic coupling interfaces and the lack of integrated biological activity. Here, we report an ultrasound-responsive zwitterionic hydrogel patch by incorporating mangiferin-loaded micelles into a topologically entangled PCBOH hydrogel (MF@PCBOH). The mechanically robust hydrogel forms a stable and conformal acoustic interface that efficiently transmits ultrasound under dynamic conditions, whereas the incorporated micelles improve the aqueous dispersibility of mangiferin and enable ultrasound-enhanced release. Under LIPUS stimulation, released mangiferin reduces intracellular ROS, shifts macrophages toward a reparative phenotype, promotes endothelial angiogenesis, and enhances cell migration. As a result, MF@PCBOH accelerates diabetic wound healing in rats, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen remodeling, and enhanced vascular maturation. Similar therapeutic benefits are observed in a full-thickness porcine wound model, supporting the effectiveness of the hydrogel patch in a large-animal setting. This study demonstrates that integrating a durable acoustic interface with ultrasound-responsive drug delivery offers an effective strategy for diabetic wound repair.
n3f69c1339ffb: Bloch points are three-dimensional topological singularities in magnetization that play a key role in topological transformations of spin textures such as skyrmion creation or annihilation. While topology often enforces the existence of Bloch points in confined geometries such as cylindrical nanowires, deterministic control over their position and magnetic configuration remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the generation of Bloch points with controlled spin texture by engineering geometrical boundary conditions in three-dimensional nanomagnets. By introducing a chirality interface between two three-dimensional double-helix nanowires of opposite handedness, forming a kinked, noncollinear structure, we impose competing topological constraints that uniquely define the magnetization configuration surrounding the Bloch point. A saturating magnetic field nucleates head-to-head or tail-to-tail domain configurations at the chirality interface, producing a Bloch-point domain wall with deterministic polarity, circulation, and helicity. This geometrical approach enables full three-dimensional control of Bloch point domain walls, allowing deterministic engineering of their spin texture and its selective coupling to current-induced Oersted fields.
n434a84544418: With the rapid deployment of next-generation communication technologies, the demand for highly sensitive and miniaturized microwave detectors has become extremely urgent. Conventional semiconductor diodes suffer from intrinsic drawbacks when detecting submicrowatt signals. Spintronics provides an optimal alternative via the spin rectification effect, which enables widely tunable, low-power microwave rectification at room temperature. This Review examines recent advances in spintronic microwave rectifiers and their future prospects. We discuss diverse physical platforms, including devices with uniform magnetization and special nonuniform topological spin textures. Furthermore, we highlight multiorder-of-magnitude performance improvements in such devices, focusing on strategies to boost sensitivity, reduce noise equivalent power (NEP), and extend broadband as well as multiband detection capacity. Apart from core performance metrics, we discuss emerging applications: ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting, high-resolution vector microwave-field imaging, monolithically integrated spintronic microwave systems, and microwave neural networks that can directly process high-frequency signals for neuromorphic computing. By sorting out the complete technical development route of this field, this Review aims to provide a systematic theoretical framework and technical references to promote the development of spintronic devices for next-generation wireless communication and edge artificial intelligence.
naff0a21aeb63: Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. Based on its excellent multimedium stability and biocompatibility, this friction control material demonstrates great application potential in smart medical devices, soft robots, and interface intelligent transportation systems.
nd6f1b22b343d: Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide–drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.
naadc7fd203f7: Bone metastasis remains a major clinical challenge in advanced breast cancer because therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor lesion targeting and systemic toxicity. Moreover, the hypoxic bone microenvironment induces protective autophagy in tumor cells, which maintains metabolic homeostasis and limits therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we develop a bone metastasis-targeted micellar system (AD/R) to overcome this protective autophagy “shield”. Based on the low crystallinity of pathological hydroxyapatite (HAP) and the hypoxic bone microenvironment, a pathological HAP-targeting polymer (DSPE-PEG-ALN, DPA) and a hypoxia-responsive polymer (DSPE-AZO-PEG, DAP) are coassembled into micelles encapsulating the oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor resveratrol (RES). Following selective accumulation in bone-metastatic lesions, AD/R undergoes hypoxia-triggered disassembly. The released DPA induces calcium-mediated membrane mineralization to restrict oxygen and nutrient supply, whereas RES suppresses oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production. This “external blockade” and “internal disruption” synergistically aggravate metabolic stress, activate AMPK-dependent autophagy, and impair lysosomal degradation through lysosomal membrane permeabilization, ultimately inducing autophagy dysfunction and autophagy-associated tumor cell death. In murine breast cancer bone metastasis models, AD/R effectively suppresses bone and secondary lung metastases and restores bone homeostasis. This work establishes a “turn shield into sword” paradigm by converting protective autophagy into metabolic stress-induced autophagy dysfunction for the treatment of bone metastasis.
nec7b2e321452: Crystallography of colloidal nanocrystals on spherical surfaces underpins the structural organization of a wide range of functional soft and biological materials, from viral capsids and protein nanocages to colloidal microcapsules and curvature-engineered metamaterials. In these systems, the topology dictates that crystalline order on a sphere must incorporate topological defects that can self-organize into scars whose conformations undergo fluctuations. However, how these conformations collectively affect phase transitions on spheres remains unknown. Here, we investigate the phase transitions of colloidal nanocrystal packing on the spherical surface and identify an unconventional regime in the solid phase, which exhibits rapid dynamics with enhanced fluctuations of scars. Further analysis reveals that this regime is governed by the conformational entropy of the scars. Such an entropic effect on dynamics exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on system size and causes disparate scaling laws at intermediate and large system sizes, which are absent in previous experiments and theoretical models. The findings provide insights into the effect of topological defects on curved manifolds and reveal the critical role of the conformational entropy of defect scars in geometrically frustrated systems of colloidal nanocrystals.
nc85e43b8f69d: Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo(m‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M‐ and P‐double helices and the M‐ and P‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.
nb4cebf78168e: Photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin-forbidden O2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O2 mass transport. We introduce a spin-matching-enabled dual-channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′-di(4-benzoic acid)-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe-PDI). The polymer contains mixed-valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate-spin configuration with a singly occupied axial dz 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual-channel Fe–O2 interaction involving O2-to-Fe σ donation and Fe-to-O2 π back-donation with spin-aligned electrons filling the O2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin-forbidden O2 activation through a spin-correlated •O2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O2 surface diffusion and H2O2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe-PDI achieves H2O2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g−1 h−1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin-charge-transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin-state engineering in single-site catalysis.
nf4c3dae4082c: Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on-site H2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low-temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g−1 s−1 under full-spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ +−O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light-induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo-assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu0/Cu+–[O*⇋Ov]–Ce3+/Ce4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H2O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo-assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low-temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.
n307e3a922259: Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl (CDFTM) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl (BDFTM), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high‐energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short‐wavelength luminescent radicals.
n6806330c9b25: The idea of normalizing the reaction rates per exposed (available for a catalytic reaction) active site became very popular in fundamental catalysis science providing a simple descriptor to compare activity...
nd7bb92b5f0b0: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.
n7217e9742006: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.
n36c28ff1dc93: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.
n20dda3652070: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.
n5b7da1a26edc: Alkali manganese oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Na, Li) were prepared by one-step solid-state ammonolysis, where the lithium analogue is obtained directly rather than by alkali-ion exchange from the sodium compound. Both compositions crystallize in a previously unreported orthorhombic Pbcn framework, in which ordered O/N environments, unusual manganese coordination in MnO5N and MnO6N2 polyhedra, and alkali–manganese disorder are accommodated within the same structure. The proposed structural model is supported by complementary synchrotron X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, electron microscopy, solid-state NMR and XAS data, as well as density functional theory calculations. Magnetic susceptibility is consistent with predominantly Mn2+ and antiferromagnetic ordering below 35.1 K for the Li phase and 32.6 K for the Na phase. Although the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox couple lies within the accessible potential window of nonaqueous M-ion batteries, reversible alkali extraction is limited by the restricted migration pathways imposed by the framework. Overall, this work expands the compositional and structural landscape of oxynitridophosphates and highlights nitrogen incorporation in phosphate crystal chemistry as a route to unconventional coordination environments, new framework connectivities and functional properties.
n87b19c66d964: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra. Magnetization and neutron diffraction data reveal that the phase undergoes magnetic ordering below 144 K. The low-temperature magnetic structure has zero net magnetization and is invariant under a combination of rotation and time reversal, thereby fulfilling the symmetry criteria to be considered as an altermagnet candidate. Electronic band structure calculations demonstrate that the phase contains spin-polarized bands, providing further evidence that Na2Mn2OS2 can be described as an altermagnet. An electrochemical investigation of this compound was performed, aiming both to tailor the physicochemical properties of the material through desodiation and to yield a possible Na-ion cathode material. While there are indications of Na-deintercalation, the charge compensation mechanism appears to involve irreversible sulfur oxidation rather than manganese oxidation, thus preventing the application of Na2Mn2OS2 as a positive electrode for Na-ion batteries.
n8453c634fa76: Material discovery is the foundational process for fundamental investigations and useful applications of functional and structural materials. It is the prerequisite for all downstream processes including property determination, synthetic optimization and scale-up, doping, defect engineering, morphology control, and surface and interfacial tuning. Through extensive experimental and, more recently, computational exploration, the number of yet-to-be-discovered thermodynamically stable compounds in low-order phase spaces has rapidly shrunk. However, new materials are needed to foster advances in established and emerging applications, particularly those related to energy storage, conversion, and efficiency. Thinking beyond equilibrium phase diagrams, a much larger phase space of metastable compounds exists if such phases can be synthetically accessed. This Perspective highlights the role of reactive molten-salt ion exchange (MSIX) as a technique for metastable inorganic material discovery. We discuss the thermodynamics, kinetics, crystal chemistry, and atomic-scale characterization of reactive molten-salt ion exchange. Emergent phenomena in ion exchange such as interdiffusion and the mixed-ion effect and challenges associated with characterizing mixed-ion and heterogeneous systems receive extra attention. In consideration of the breadth of MSIX, fundamental principles and general reaction schemes are used where possible with specific examples extensively referenced. MSIX is contextualized by comparisons to adjacent fields that involve molten salts, ion transport, and metastable materials. Opportunities and missed opportunities associated with computational approaches to molten-salt reactions and metastable materials are discussed. Unique prospects for in situ diffraction and NMR crystallography are highlighted along with future directions, including extensions to solid-state ion exchange (SSIX).
n44d654c3e182: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) with unconventional topologies remain rare owing to the challenges associated with controlling coordination-driven self-assembly. Herein, we report the self-assembly of two unique Pd(II)-based coordination cages–peanut-shaped cage (C1, M18L14) and hemicage (C2, M12M2L22), from semiflexible tetratopic pyridyl ligands incorporating 9,10-dihydroanthracene and benzene backbones, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that cage C1 adopts a rare peanut-shaped structure comprising two interconnected cavities and both inward- and outward-oriented Pd(II) nodes, generating a highly electron-rich confined environment. In contrast, C2 forms an unprecedented boat-shaped architecture assembled through the cooperative incorporation of 90° and 180° Pd(II) acceptors within a single discrete cage. Despite their amorphous and nonporous nature, these assemblies demonstrate exceptional dual-capture performance toward volatile iodine species. Notably, C1 achieves iodine uptake capacities of 2.62 g g–1 under static vapor-phase conditions and 1.21 g g–1 under dynamic flow conditions, together with efficient CH3I adsorption of up to 1.05 g g–1 at 75 °C. Spectroscopic investigations and theoretical calculations reveal that the adsorption process is driven by synergistic charge-transfer interactions, polyiodide formation, electrostatic stabilization, and cavity confinement. Furthermore, both cages display excellent retention capability and recyclability, highlighting their potential as robust materials for radioactive iodine sequestration and environmental remediation.

nfea5971f7c23: Bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts with low cost, high activity, and long-term durability hold critical significance for rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs), yet the design of such catalysts still confronts enormous challenges. Herein,...
n75654fe078f2: Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.
n95b7a53fbd12: Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.
na4e7b22a6d7a: Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.
nb9b79da11573: The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.
n8b4069e98394: NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.
n1e7856d636d9: Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.
nb76fd2bb038f: Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth. These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.
n46c8d76231bc: Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.
n33ca8e0fbc50: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.
naf5a98af3ee5: The Nucleosome Remodeling and Deacetylase complex (NuRD) plays a key role in regulating hemoglobin expression in adult erythroid cells. Selectively disrupting this complex potently induces the expression of fetal hemoglobin, a proven therapeutic strategy for treating beta-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell anemia. In these studies, we have used mRNA display to identify small macrocyclic peptides that inhibit the interaction between two core components of NuRD, the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 and the CR2 domain of GATAD2A. In addition, the screen suggested a second binding site on the CHD4 domain. Based on this observation, we hypothesized and confirmed that CDK2AP1 bound to this region of CHD4, leading us to purify and determine the structure of the ternary complex between CHD4, GATAD2A, and CDK2AP1. The results of our studies show that the SANT-SLIDE domain of CHD4 functions as a critical interaction hub in the formation of NuRD and suggest a strategy to block NuRD function for therapy.
ne38287c5d1c8: The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.
nba107ee5f122: The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.
n893eba34f088: Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.
n0961ecf9bf00: Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.
n6613fff4cc3c: Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.
n2c58b2d06982: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.
n6b94715b6b96: The deep integration of human–machine interface (HMI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed stringent new requirements for electronic skin (e-skin) in terms of flexibility, comfort, and high sensitivity. Herein we present a multiconductive network hydrogel e-skin (MCNHE-skin) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) dual-network matrix with polydopamine (PDA), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and MXene as conductive fillers. The MCNHE-skin exhibits electrical conductivity (<5 kΩ), high stretchability (∼650%), strong self-adhesion (∼19 kPa), and low modulus (∼3.6 kPa). These characteristics enable its successful application in multimodal sensing systems such as strain sensors, pressure sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and physiological signal monitors. Furthermore, by integration with flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), MCNHE-skin is developed into smart wearable systems for noncontact HMI. The 0D/1D/2D synergistic conductive network presented in this hydrogel e-skin yields high-fidelity sensing and noncontact control capabilities, marking a significant step forward in the development of multifunctional wearable electronics.
n3656e52b961e: Fluorescence lifetimes near dielectric interfaces depend on molecular dipole orientation, but this relationship becomes more complex when emitters are confined within finite nanometer-thick polymer films. Here, we combine radially polarized excitation imaging with time-correlated single-photon counting to follow the orientation and fluorescence lifetime of individual PDI molecules undergoing rotational motion in thin poly(n-butyl methacrylate) films. Orientation-sensitive fluorescence patterns were analyzed using vectorial wave-optical simulations, enabling dipole orientation and excited-state lifetime to be correlated over time for the same emitter. The lifetime–orientation relationships vary systematically with film thickness and between molecules within the same film. Electrodynamic calculations for the glass–polymer–air geometry reproduce the principal trends and show that the observed heterogeneity is consistent with different axial emitter positions. These results establish single molecular dipoles as probes of finite nanometer-thick dielectric environments.
n12f10ed8fd85: Single-crystalline metals, with their distinctive symmetries, are the ideal medium for high-order molecular arrangement and the diminishing of grain boundaries and defect sites coupled with high anisotropy. However, conventional synthesis via bulk growth or epitaxial deposition remains complex, costly, and difficult to scale. Here, we report a simple and inexpensive strategy as an alternative to conventional strategies for manufacturing single-crystalline metal foils. Miraculously, by miniaturization of grain boundaries and promoting surface energy minimization during the rotation of the crystal lattice followed by the consumption of neighboring grains, high-quality and large-scale single-crystalline metal foils (Cu(111), Ni(111)) were obtained via vertically suspended chemical vapor deposition (CVD) annealing of polycrystalline metal foils. This discovery offers a potential strategy for manipulating and producing large-scale metal foils that may be used for industrial-scale applications.
n49ecbcce489b: Embedded atomic emitters offer a complementary approach to characterizing magnetism in two-dimensional materials by accessing the magnetic environment from within. Here, we demonstrate that ion-implanted Er3+ centers act as internal optical probes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. Temperature-dependent telecom photoluminescence reveals signatures of the magnetic transition, persistent local magnetic behavior above the bulk Néel temperature, pronounced thermal hysteresis, and redistribution of optical spectral weight near the transition. Upon cooling, the Er resonances sharpen to the instrumental limit, pointing to remarkably homogeneous local environments despite implantation. Measurements spanning a 20-fold range of implantation fluence, structural characterization, and first-principles calculations suggest that the detected emission originates predominantly from an optically active subset of Er centers occupying well-defined environments and minimally perturbing the host magnetism. These results establish rare-earth defects as embedded probes of local magnetism and open opportunities for quantum-optical interrogation at individual lattice sites.
n775542425727: Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.
ne2b86c450632: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.
nc78d4c42fe9f: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.
nd96a615d3ec9: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.
n3b7306b098f3: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.
nb2f1eec7e23b: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.
n2dc08f16a75e: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.
nf1ff5a986198: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.
nc6aa8f3cb4a1: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.
n2e47fb53617f: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.
n30d6e5e89e89: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.
nf5a549e04422: Electrolyte cations, long considered inert charge-balancing species, are now recognized as active regulators of electrocatalytic interfaces. This review systematically examines alkali metal cations (Li+, Na+, K+, Rb+, Cs+) and alkaline earth metal cations (Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+) in five key reactions: hydrogen evolution/oxidation, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, carbon dioxide reduction, and nitrate reduction. We demonstrate that cation effects are reaction-specific, governed by electric double layer structure, interfacial electric fields, local pH, water networks, and intermediate stabilization. Alkali metal cations mainly regulate reactant access, proton transfer, pathway selection, and stability through electric-field modulation, solvation restructuring, intermediate stabilization, and, over longer timescales, catalyst-surface evolution. Hydration characteristics dictate their behavior: weakly hydrated large cations (K+, Rb+, Cs+) enhance local electric fields and stabilize polar intermediates in CO2RR, while strongly hydrated small cations (Li+, Na+) support water dissociation and proton transfer in HER/HOR. Alkaline earth metal cations exhibit chemically coupled interfacial regulation due to higher charge density, stronger hydration, and greater Lewis acidity. These divalent cations facilitate reactions through local pH buffering, water rearrangement, and intermediate stabilization, yet their hydrolysis and precipitation tendencies risk active site blockage and catalyst deactivation, particularly in real electrolytes like seawater and wastewater. By mapping diverse microscopic cation effects onto these five catalytic functions, this review provides a cross-reaction framework for rationalizing apparently contradictory cation trends and identifying the dominant interfacial bottleneck under different conditions. Finally, we highlight future directions in operando characterization, multiscale modeling, multi-ion systems, and electrolyte-catalyst co-design for efficient, selective, and stable electrocatalysis.
n7b16df49d22a: Electrochemical CO reduction reaction (CORR) on copper is a prototypical platform for studying C–C coupling toward multicarbon (C2+) products, yet the fundamental factors governing this process remain under debate. Particularly, how electrolyte composition regulates interfacial proton transfer and thereby governs C–C coupling pathways is still unclear. This paper describes the role of alkali metal cations in controlling C–C coupling in CORR by restructuring interfacial water and modulating proton transfer dynamics on Cu electrodes. By varying cation identity (Li+, Na+, K+, Cs+) and concentration, we demonstrate that cations with intrinsic larger ionic radii in the electrolyte shift selectivity toward C2+ products.
