Combining differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) analysis with in situ surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) and attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) investigations, it is revealed that alkali metal cations with large intrinsic radii have weak hydration shells that disrupt the interfacial hydrogen-bond (H-bond) network and increase the population of cation-coordinated water molecules at the interface, which may serve as more effective proton transfer channels toward surface intermediates. This reconstruction of interfacial water can accelerate *CO hydrogenation, thus promoting the C–C coupling for C2+ production. These findings identify interfacial water as an active regulator of interfacial proton transfer, thereby supporting a mechanistic link between electrolyte composition and C–C coupling pathways. This work emphasizes the importance of the interfacial microenvironment and molecular-level understanding of electrochemical reactions.
ndb73c3f1a23a: Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed deconstructive oxygenation platform for the direct conversion of unstrained N-unsubstituted cyclic amines into versatile β-, γ-, and δ-aminoketones. The product diversity is achieved by adjusting the substituents at the β- or γ-position of cyclic amines that proceed through single or consecutive C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond cleavage, respectively. Following this method, we achieved skeletal modification of unstrained cyclic amines through ring contraction or atom replacement, leading to rapid structural diversification of cyclic amines. The synthetic utility of this method was further demonstrated by the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, fluoxetine, atomoxetine, and norfluoxetine. Control experiments indicated that, in the presence of the co-oxidant nitroxyl, the copper-catalyzed sequential dehydrogenative oxidation followed by single-electron transfer-induced aerobic oxygenative C–C bond cleavage was responsible for this effective transformation.
ne28d65103078: Commercialization of electrochemical nitrogen reduction (eNRR) is hindered by limited catalyst performance, the lack of scalable electrochemical cell architectures, and an incomplete understanding of performance-limiting processes. This work aims to address these challenges through a systematic investigation of catalyst composition and microstructure, device configuration, and reaction mechanisms. Molybdenum (Mo) metal single atoms and clusters supported on mesoporous nitrogen-doped carbon were synthesized with tunable pore sizes via a five-second photothermal pyrolysis of a self-assembled bottlebrush block copolymer (BBCP) template. For eNRR, improved Mo dispersion enhanced electrochemical accessibility, while the coexistence of atomically dispersed Mo species and Mo clusters produced a structurally heterogeneous catalytic environment that benefits eNRR. A gas-diffusion electrode (GDE) flow cell was constructed for continuous operation testing; the catalyst–device system achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 21.6% and an ammonia yield rate of 34.7 μg h–1 mg–1. Intermediate pore sizes and balanced electrode wettability promoted effective triple-phase boundary formation and active-site utilization. Electrochemical characterization combined with machine-learning analysis of flow-cell parameters indicated that activation polarization is the dominant loss mechanism, governed primarily by intrinsic active-site kinetics and electrochemically accessible surface area. In contrast, pore size, metal dispersion, and electrode wettability primarily regulate site accessibility rather than mass-transport limitations. Together, these results provide a framework linking catalyst structure, electrode architecture, and kinetic limitations in eNRR flow-cell systems and offer practical design guidelines for advancing scalable eNRR technology.
ne6813bddcde6: Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have emerged as a highly desirable system for grid storage applications due to low-cost, high-energy density, and safe operating conditions. While AZMB studies often focus on functional mitigation of dendrite formation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), corrosion remains a more ambiguous yet crucial limiting factor in anode performance. Specifically, recent work points to persistent chemical corrosion as a major source of resting capacity loss in AZMBs. In this work, we present a wide-ranging mechanism for galvanic corrosion based on fundamental electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, highlighting the key roles of battery components, electrolyte conditions, and other contributing factors. Importantly, this mechanistic framework also applies when plating and stripping Zn on the anode, offering additional insight into the ever-elusive mechanistic origins of HER during those operating regimes. We then propose several promising avenues of inquiry and methods for further predicting, understanding, and mitigating corrosion in AZMBs.
n646b78aa0dd7: Triangular metal-oxo nodes are widely employed as catalytic motifs in metal–organic frameworks. Photocatalytic N2 fixation using the all-iron nodes can be switched off by replacing them with all-chromium nodes. However, the two nodes bind N2 in the opposite order to their activity. The present contribution shows that the electronic structure of the metal, which governs the small-molecule binding to the framework, determines the magnetic exchange topology of the [MIII3(μ3-O)] node. Combining broken-symmetry and non-collinear DFT, Hamiltonian-based reconstruction of Mössbauer spectra, and quantitative modeling of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, one finds that FeIII exhibits a genuinely frustrated triangle of comparable antiferromagnetic interactions, whereas CrIII features an asymmetric dimer-plus-monomer governed by unusually strong biquadratic interaction, placing it outside the conventional Heisenberg regime. The distinct electronic structure is reflected in markedly different magnetic topologies and N2 binding strengths, rationalizing the contrasting photocatalytic activities of the two frameworks. These results establish magnetic exchange topology as an experimentally accessible descriptor of chemical function in trinuclear MOF nodes.
n665c5f02f781: Coordinated delivery of therapeutics with distinct physicochemical properties remains a fundamental challenge in drug design. This difficulty often stems from incompatible assembly kinetics, in which mismatched assembly behaviors among components lead to disordered structures and hinder functional integration. Here, we report a cascade assembly strategy to construct core–shell microassemblies (MTX@HPTD) by capturing transient intermediate states, enabling sequential structural organization and functional integration for spatiotemporal drug release. Upon solvent exchange, methotrexate (MTX) and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (HP) coassemble, thereby allowing the capture of an intermediate in which a dense MTX-rich core forms while the surrounding HP shell remains accessible for subsequent integration. This enables covalent anchoring of ROS-scavenging TEMPO-doped polydopamine nanoparticles (TPDA) into the evolving shell of the intermediate assembly via dynamic covalent bonding. The resulting core–shell microassemblies, featuring an MTX-rich reservoir stabilized by a functionalized HP-rich shell that entraps the TPDA payload, exhibit spatially segregated compartments, enabling diffusion-controlled release of MTX and stimuli-responsive release of TPDA. Moreover, by utilizing changes in the size of microassemblies during release, this system addresses the size-dependent trade-off between retention and uptake. In a psoriasis model, microneedle-mediated delivery achieves coordinated therapy, suppressing ferroptosis, necroptosis, and HMGB1 signaling, thereby mitigating disease severity. This work establishes the temporal capture of transient states as a promising strategy for constructing hierarchical materials for spatiotemporal release.
n772293ee5006: Performance of tandem junction nanowire (NW) solar cells relies on the electronic quality of the tunnel diodes which serve as the separating junctions between subcells. Yet, the relevant interfacial physics occurs below the optical diffraction limit. Here we use hyperspectral tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) to map, with nanoscale precision, axially defined heterojunctions in InP/InGaP tandem junction photovoltaic NWs. By resolving mode-specific phonon and phonon–plasmon responses, we show that the nominally abrupt p/p++ and p++/n++ junctions are compositionally graded. The TOM mode, used as the primary compositional marker, yields transition widths of ∼90–120 nm, whereas other lattice- and carrier-sensitive modes exhibit broader central widths up to ∼190 nm, reflecting their additional sensitivity to alloying, structural disorder, and electronic coupling. In a first-order approximation, rescaling these TERS-derived widths to shorter, device-relevant NWs yields narrower junctions, consistent with independent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements that qualitatively capture the same trend despite surface and tip convolution effects. Complementary equilibrium band-edge model combined with a simplified one-dimensional Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) calculation, as an illustrative trend, further indicates that such grading is expected to widen the effective tunnel barrier. These findings establish mode-selective hyperspectral TERS as a validated, noninvasive method for quantitative nanoscale mapping of compositional grading in III–V NW junctions, with the carrier-sensitive L1 phonon–plasmon response providing complementary, model-assisted insight into the electronic evolution of the junctions.
n88759cb66d56: All-solid-state Li batteries operating at high current densities exceeding 10 mA cm–2 are desired for high-power and rapid-charging batteries. Therefore, battery development needs to focus on reducing the electrolyte–electrode interface resistance at high current density, which is a major contributor to internal resistance. However, methods for reducing the electrolyte–electrode interfacial resistance at high current densities remain unexplored. Here, we demonstrate charge–discharge operation at 30 mA cm–2 using Li3PS4, LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, and Li metal as a solid electrolyte, 5 V-class positive electrode, and negative electrode, respectively. The introduction of Li3PO4 buffer layers at both Li–Li3PS4 and Li3PS4–LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 interfaces reduced the interfacial resistance 45,000-fold. Furthermore, the introduction of a 5 nm-thick Pt layer instead of Li3PO4 at the Li–Li3PS4 interface enabled charge–discharge operation under high-current-density conditions. This quantitative study highlights the importance of designing electrochemically robust negative electrode and electrolyte interfaces for high-power 5 V-class all-solid-state Li batteries.
n1448593c37d1: Fe-containing Ni oxyhydroxides are among the most active alkaline oxygen evolution catalysts, whose structures and performances strongly depend on precursor reconstruction and Fe location. However, achieving precise control over precursor design, reconstruction, and Fe incorporation remains highly challenging. Here, we report the low-temperature synthesis of intermetallic Ni2In3 nanoparticles as a precursor and uncover their in situ reconstruction behavior modulated by electrolyte concentration. Compared with similarly sized Ni nanoparticle-derived catalysts, the Ni2In3-derived catalysts exhibit significantly enhanced activity and stability. The optimal catalyst, after activation in 6 M KOH with Fe spiking, requires an overpotential of only 284 mV for 10 mA cm–2, along with a low Tafel slope of 31 mV dec–1. Combined electrochemical analyses, in situ/ex situ characterizations, and theoretical calculations reveal that In leaching induces electronic structure modulation and surface undercoordinated site enrichment, thereby facilitating interfacial Fe incorporation to form NiFe active centers. In an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the catalyst demonstrates excellent stability of 260 h at 1 A cm–2 at 80 °C. These findings highlight the importance of electrolyte- and precursor-dependent reconstruction in modulating the electronic structure and promoting interfacial Fe incorporation, thereby enabling the design of oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.
n328fe8e09ea3: Hyperlactatemia is a critical indicator of tissue hypoperfusion, metabolic dysfunction, and an adverse prognosis in critically ill patients. Yet conventional monitoring depends entirely on intermittent, invasive blood sampling, which cannot capture the dynamic metabolic fluctuations required to guide timely clinical interventions. Herein, we report a wearable sweat-sensing device built on a dual-diffusion-limiting architecture for the continuous and accurate assessment of clinical hyperlactatemia. This system synergistically modulates lactate diffusion in sweat through a silane-network-encapsulated lactate oxidase layer coupled to a polyvinyl chloride layer. This design effectively delays enzyme saturation, extending the linear detection range for sweat lactate to 0–60 mM and thereby fulfilling the stringent requirements of critical care monitoring. The device also integrates real-time pH and temperature calibration to safeguard measurement accuracy in complex physiological environments. Moreover, linear mixed-effects analysis of 82 paired samples from 33 critically ill patients demonstrated a strong association between sweat and blood lactate levels, with a marginal R2 of 0.840. Sweat lactate effectively identified hyperlactatemia and predicted in-hospital mortality, yielding areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.943 and 0.785, respectively. The integrated iontophoresis-microfluidics module further ensures high consistency with bedside arterial blood gas analysis, as validated by a marginal R2 of 0.811. Together, these results establish sweat biosensors as a promising platform for continuous metabolic monitoring, resuscitation assessment, and objective prognostic stratification in critical care settings.
n12e162a45ea9: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H2O activity and regulate Zn2+ desolvation through hydrogen‐bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn2+ coordination. A series of C2–C6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C4, EOD = 0.022 Å−3, MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery‐enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm−2 with 1 mAh cm−2, and the Zn||I2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.
nc143c8fe2741: Low‐frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self‐powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double‐sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM‐TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long‐term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM‐TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self‐powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.
n1ef0f4423759: Piezo-photoelectrochemical (Piezo-PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water-splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn–Teller effect-driven strategy to regulate the local B-site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO3 for efficient Piezo-PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn3+ ions with asymmetric eg orbital occupancy (t2g 3eg 1), a local MnO6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn–Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non-centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water-splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO-6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 52.3 pm V−1. This work reveals that Jahn–Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo-polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo-PEC water-splitting systems.
n73e54754107f: High‐efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor‐acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk‐heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo‐ and hetero‐intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well‐known indacenodithieno[3,2‐b]thiophene‐based (ITIC‐series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene‐based (IEICO‐series) acceptors, and state‐of‐the‐art Y‐series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo‐interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine‐tune their hetero‐interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo‐interactions while minimizing hetero‐interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature‐reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo‐ and hetero‐interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.
nf206820a8784: High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel‐free hole‐selective interface material based on phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole self‐assembled monolayers (Ph‐nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure‐property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph‐5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried‐interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me‐4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph‐5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel‐free interface enables a closed‐loop recycling route unavailable to nickel‐based devices, with recycled‐ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity‐related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.
nb4a64af6ed02: Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO3RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO3RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO3RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO3RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO3RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH3 synthesis.
n0f90bda46b28: Biomass-derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost-effective anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non-metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through-pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl-rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen-containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC-derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na+ storage domains. Consequently, the optimized HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 375.3 mAh g− 1 at 20 mA g− 1. A 700 mAh pouch cell pairing this HC with sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7, NFPP) delivers 150 Wh kg− 1 based on the combined active-material mass of both electrodes and retains 97.8% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a viable route for converting impurity-rich agricultural waste into high-performance HC anodes for practical sodium-ion energy storage.
na6ba61769243: Metasurfaces have revolutionized the optical field due to their exceptional wavefront shaping capabilities, boosting the multi‐dimensional light‐field manipulation and emission control. However, the incoherent, omnidirectional, unpolarized, and phase‐random nature of fluorescence emission limits the applicability of conventional metasurface multiplexing strategies, posing significant challenges for photoluminescence (PL) encoding and multi‐dimensional light‐emitting metasurface (LEM)‐based display technology. Here, the PL angular‐multiplexing is proposed and experimentally demonstrated based on unidirectional emission control for multi‐dimensional meta‐display. By exploiting the inherent numerical aperture limitation of the detection system and coupling PL into the guided mode via an on‐chip metasurface, the LEM‐empowered precise emission angle control is transferred into the angular‐multiplexed intensity encoding degree of freedom, enabling a dual‐channel PL meta‐display. Furthermore, by incorporating directional multiplexing, the multi‐dimensional LEM achieves four independent PL images corresponding to distinct observation angles and illumination directions. This PL angular‐multiplexing approach, together with the multi‐dimensional meta‐display architecture, significantly expands the multiplexing encoding capability of fluorescence light‐field manipulation, offering promising opportunities for diverse applications, including next‐generation optical display/encryption techniques, biological sensing, and incoherent illumination engineering.
ndd765432eef7: Multilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), with their tunable layer numbers and stacking configurations, provide a key platform for designing electronic and optical properties beyond the monolayer limit, promising to drive the development of next‐generation semiconductor technologies. However, the promise of multilayer TMDs remains limited by the lack of scalable synthesis routes that enable large‐area growth with precise control over thickness, stacking sequence, and material quality. From the perspective of energy competition during the growth process, we systematically analyze four principal growth paradigms: layer‐by‐layer epitaxy, step‐edge‐guided‐growth, hypotaxy (‘hypo’ meaning downward and ‘taxy’ meaning arrangement), and interfacial epitaxy, while also outlining corresponding improvement strategies for each paradigm. Looking forward, we discuss the future trajectory of the field, highlighting the viable routes to evolve from the current paradigm of imprecise kinetic control to one of atomically precise fabrication. This perspective not only furnishes tangible strategies but also provides promising directions for achieving the controlled, scalable production of large‐area multilayer TMDs.
n464d2b1587f3: Severe ischemic diseases are driven by oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Macrophage‐derived extracellular vesicles (M2‐EVs) offer substantial regenerative potential, yet their clinical translation is hindered by microenvironmental degradation and a lack of targeting. We developed an engineered bio‐nano hybrid platform (M2‐EVs@CDs‐TPP) by integrating triphenylphosphonium (TPP)‐functionalized carbon dots (CDs) with M2‐EVs. This design enables a dual‐localization mode, wherein CDs‐TPP act as an antioxidant shield on the vesicle surface to enhance cellular uptake, while also serving as a subcellular navigator to precisely direct the therapeutic payload to damaged mitochondria. Mechanistically, the system exerts a dual‐action therapeutic effect. It chemically scavenges pathogenic mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) to disrupt the ROS‐induced ROS release (RIRR) cycle. Concurrently, this relief of oxidative stress synergizes with M2‐EVs to activate the Nrf2‐PGC‐1α metabolic regulatory hub. This biological reprogramming establishes robust biphasic antioxidant defenses (via HO‐1 and SOD2) and drives mitochondrial biogenesis (via NRF1/TFAM), reestablishing cellular ATP homeostasis. In vitro and in a murine critical limb ischemia model, this metabolic rewiring drove multidimensional tissue regeneration, encompassing angiogenesis, myoblast differentiation, and anti‐inflammatory macrophage polarization. This work provides a modular engineering strategy to overcome translational barriers of native EVs and highlights the clinical potential of targeting mitochondrial metabolism for pan‐ischemic disease therapy.
n59c51feb7ebc: Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries are the ultimate anode configuration for high-energy-density energy storage, yet their practical adoption is hindered by uncontrolled Li dendrite growth. Here, we present a dual-sided regulation strategy that homogenizes Li deposition through simultaneous bottom-up and top-down control. At the current collector, an ultrathin platinum (Pt) layer leverages its lithiophilicity to stabilize nucleation and promote dense bottom growth. At the separator, an amorphous tantalum oxide (a-TaO x ) ceramic layer exploits thermodynamic Li dewetting to suppress upward dendritic propagation, enforcing top-down uniformity. This synergistic Pt/a-TaO x dual-interface design orchestrates Li deposition across the entire electrode, enabling stable cycling at high cathode areal capacities (4.78 mAh cm–2) with 70% capacity retention after 110 cycles in an anode-less configuration (N/P ratio = 0) and 80% after 187 cycles with pre-lithiation (N/P ratio = 0.42). By transcending conventional bottom-only protection, this work establishes a new framework for stabilizing Li deposition across the full thickness in high-capacity anode-less Li metal batteries.
ne03b080ed4ef: High‐temperature dielectric films are essential components for capacitive energy storage in severe environments, ranging from hybrid electric vehicles to power systems. However, the surge in leakage current at elevated temperatures leads to a dramatic decrease in discharge energy efficiency, falling well short of the requirements for the next‐generation high‐temperature polymer dielectrics. Herein, a novel technology of “melting extrusion‐hot stretching‐quenching” was utilized to generate high‐temperature polycarbonate (HTPC)‐based dielectric films, where the compatible blends of polymethyl methacrylate/polyvinylidene fluoride (PMMA/PVDF) were in situ formed into highly aligned microfibrils. The well‐designed microfibrils enhanced the interfacial polarization and efficiently served as carrier traps, thereby synergistically improving the discharge energy density and discharge energy efficiency at high temperature. Consequently, the as‐prepared all‐organic dielectric film exhibited an appreciable discharge energy density as high as 6.54 J/cm3 with a discharge energy efficiency of 87.5% at 600 MV/m and 120°C. After being continuously charged and discharged at 300 MV/m and 120°C for 105 times, a negligible attenuation was observed in energy storage properties. This work provides a feasible way to tailor the comprehensive performance of HTPC by internally constructing oriented microfibril structure, thereby advancing the design and scalable fabrication of HTPC‐engineered dielectric films for high‐temperature energy storage.
n0e8279d3d547: Uterine scarring after cesarean section is a major cause of secondary infertility and uterine rupture, and its formation is closely associated with disruption of the mechanical microenvironment at incision sites, yet its mechanobiological basis and effective mechano‐regulatory therapies remain poorly defined. We identify focal adhesion kinase (FAK)‐mediated mechanotransduction as a key driver of post‐cesarean uterine scar formation. To target this process, we developed FAK‐PTC‐Lipo@MN, a biodegradable microneedle patch composed of gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and ε‐poly‐L‐lysine‐glycidyl methacrylate (EPLGMA), enabling sustained local delivery of FAK‐PROTAC‐loaded liposomes. In a rat cesarean‐section model, FAK‐PTC‐Lipo@MN reduced inflammatory infiltration, collagen deposition, myometrial thickening, and tissue stiffness, thereby suppressing uterine scar formation. Transcriptomic analysis further showed a shift of uterine repair mode from fibrotic toward regenerative repair, with activation of Wnt/Notch‐related pathways and downregulation of ECM‐associated fibrotic signaling. Functionally, FAK‐PTC‐Lipo@MN promoted uterine functional recovery and improved key reproductive outcomes (e.g., conception time, fetal number, and fetal weight) after cesarean section. Mechanistically, released FAK‐PTC‐Lipo induced FAK degradation and inhibited its activation, thereby reducing F‐actin polymerization, cell traction forces, ECM remodeling and tension, and N‐cadherin‐dependent fibroblast collective migration. This study establishes FAK‐targeted mechanotherapy as a promising strategy for uterine incision regeneration and reproductive function restoration after cesarean section.
n1903bb522226: During long‐term operation, repeated thermal expansion and contraction inevitably generate cyclic thermal stresses that cause dielectric film buckling, cracking, and eventual device failure. As promising candidates for next‐generation dielectric films, polyimides (PIs) are therefore required to combine high energy‐storage performance with mechanical fatigue resistance under coupled thermal, electrical, and mechanical stresses. Here, we report a mechanically interlocked crosslinked topology designed to meet this requirement. A maleimide‐functionalized crown ether monomer (CM) forms mechanically interlocked junctions with PI chains, while co‐crosslinking with a bismaleimide monomer (SiMI) extends these junctions into a three‐dimensional network and creates nanoscale multiphase interfaces through SiMI self‐crosslinking. This topology improves high‐temperature energy‐storage performance and imparts strong mechanical integrity to the PI films, especially resistance to mechanical fatigue. Dielectric‐optimized PI‐CM0.75‐M7.5 achieves a breakdown strength of 600 MV/m at 200°C and maintains η ≥ 90% up to 450 MV/m. Mechanically optimized PI‐CM0.25‐M2.5 shows a Young's modulus of 2.9 GPa and a stable cyclic mechanical response, with only 5.8% stress decay after 50 tensile loading‐unloading cycles and a peak stress that approaches a plateau during cycling. This work provides a topology‐guided strategy for balancing thermal stability, high‐temperature dielectric energy storage, and cyclic mechanical reliability in polymer dielectrics.
n6f6f2da31715: Time‐of‐flight neutron and high‐energy x‐ray diffraction, together with Raman spectroscopy performed on tiny splat‐quenched GeS droplets (2.6 mg total), supported by first‐principles molecular dynamics and DFT modeling of vibrational properties, were employed to decipher the atomic and electronic structure of this promising OTS material for next‐generation high‐density memory architectures. A half‐century‐old structural controversy, between a continuous 4:2 random network of tetrahedra and a distorted trigonal model derived from orthorhombic GeS, is resolved, revealing instead a patchwork of mixed tetrahedral and trigonal units. Finite‐field FPMD simulations predict that, under a high electric field driving the ON state, a mild structural transformation begins, characterized by a partial conversion of mixed tetrahedra into strongly deformed defect‐octahedral units with elongated interatomic distances and a reduced population of Ge─Ge homopolar bonds. The simulations reveal that emerging under‐ and over‐coordinated Ge and S species, accompanied by three‐membered rings, form an interconnected defect network associated with overlapping, localized, and extended mid‐gap states near the Fermi level and with bandgap closure. These computational results suggest that the resulting donor‐like and acceptor‐like centers and amphoteric defect sites enable high‐rate electron hopping and tunneling, thereby generating strong electrical contrast between the low‐conducting OFF and highly conductive ON states.
nf1139f37586d: While tumor cells exhibit a well‐known dependence on glucose, effectively exploiting this vulnerability has been challenging. Achieving sustained and intensive glucose consumption and overcoming tumor metabolic adaptability as well as compensatory angiogenesis remain unsolved problems. This study developed a disassemblable, self‐enhancing nanoreactor (GCG). The design centers on a positive feedback loop built upon the glucose transporter GLUT1. GCG is efficiently internalized by hijacking GLUT1, which is overexpressed on tumor cells. Once inside the tumor‐specific high‐glutathione (GSH) environment, it disassembles and activates glucose oxidase (GOx), leading to rapid intracellular glucose depletion. This deprived state, in turn, induces up‐regulation of GLUT1 expression in tumor cells, recruiting more GCG nanoreactors and establishing a self‐enhancing cycle of glucose deprivation. These results indicated that this strategy enabled rapid and sustained glucose consumption in the oxygen‐rich superficial regions of tumors, thereby cutting off the nutrient supply to deeper tumor areas and successfully inducing disulfidptosis via NADPH exhaustion. Concurrently, the resulting extreme glucose scarcity effectively inhibited endothelial cell sprouting and migration, achieving synergistic anti‐angiogenesis. Consequently, this self‐enhancing metabolic intervention exhibited superior tumor suppression (87% inhibition) and anti‐metastatic efficacy. Importantly, it presents a promising therapeutic strategy for tumor therapy by orchestrating self‐enhancing glucose deprivation.
n74ad4406dfd0: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into materials discovery is hindered by the trade‐off between exploration breadth and exploitation depth, while the lack of embedded domain knowledge and systematic chemical space compression further limits intelligent materials exploration under data scarcity. Herein, we propose a literature‐knowledge‐directed iterative workflow that combines large language models (LLMs) with Bayesian optimization (BO) for the rational electrolyte design for ultra‐stable sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). LLMs serve as auxiliary tools for knowledge mining, while BO accelerates multi‐objective optimization to obtain electrolyte compositions. The optimized dual‐anion hybrid solvation electrolyte (DHSE) constructs a synergistic solvation structure, which induces the formation of a compact, inorganic‐rich, and mechanically robust cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). The as‐formed CEI layer suppresses parasitic side reactions and accelerates Na+ transport by reducing the desolvation barrier. Remarkably, industrial‐scale Ah‐level hard carbon||NaNi0.3Mn0.3Fe0.3O2 pouch cells assembled with DHSE deliver a high energy density of 107.7 Wh kg−1, alongside a superior capacity retention of 94% after 100 cycles at 0.5C. This work not only develops a high‐performance electrolyte for practically applicable SIBs but also provides a general human‐agent collaborative framework for intelligent materials development under data‐limited conditions.
nf072c6655b40: Manganese‐based layered oxides are promising cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their practical deployment is restricted by Mn3+‐induced Jahn‐Teller distortion, irreversible high‐voltage P2‐O2 phase transitions, and oxygen‐related side reactions that collectively cause structural deterioration and rapid capacity fading. Here, based on literature‐correlation analysis of reported Ni─Mn P2‐type cathodes, we establish a machine‐learning‐guided dopant‐class design strategy. The analysis reveals distinct roles of metal, non‐metal, and metalloid dopants in governing cycling stability and redox reversibility, identifying metalloid regulation as the most favorable direction for enhancing high‐voltage structural and redox stability. Guided by this insight, an Al─B─F co‐doped P2‐type cathode is rationally designed, in which boron reinforces the oxygen framework through strong B─O covalency, while Al and F provide complementary cationic and anionic regulation. The optimized cathode delivers 142.8 mAh g−1 at a high average voltage of 3.53 V and exhibits superior low‐temperature capacity retention of 98.19% after 300 cycles at −5 C. In situ XRD, soft x‐ray absorption spectroscopy, ex situ XPS, operando DEMS, and DFT calculations reveal a highly reversible reaction pathway featuring stabilized oxygen redox and near‐zero volumetric strain (ΔV/V ≈ 0.025%). This work establishes machine‐learning‐guided dopant‐class design as a general strategy for developing durable high‐voltage layered sodium‐ion cathodes.
n34ddf516f625: Li‐S batteries (LSBs) are emerging as formidable contenders in the field of energy storage systems, owing to their cost‐effectiveness and ultrahigh energy density that surpasses that of conventional Li‐ion batteries. Nonetheless, unresolved issues, such as Li dendrite growth and parasitic chemical reactions between the Li metal and dissolved polysulfides, pose significant safety concerns and remain major hurdles to their commercial viability. Herein, we propose a Li‐rich In3Li13 intermetallic alloy anode (In‐Li IMA) fabricated via a simple roll‐pressing and pressure‐holding process. Unlike previous studies that focused primarily on stabilized interfaces for dendrite suppression, the in situ‐formed In‐Li IMA demonstrates not only significantly inhibited dendritic Li growth but also minimized volume change during cycling, owing to its ionically and electronically conductive 3D framework. Furthermore, simulation studies reveal that the In‐Li IMA suppresses polysulfide‐induced side reactions due to its hole‐dominated conduction and weaker polysulfide adsorption energy relative to Li. In contrast to the control Li cell that exhibits significant capacity fading, the In‐Li IMA cell achieves 87.4% capacity retention over 600 cycles and exhibits improved cyclability even in large‐area pouch‐cell configurations. Based on this accessible approach for fabricating large‐scale multifunctional anodes, this study provides critical design insights for developing practical anodes for LSBs.
n4452a9a37632: Two‐dimensional (2D) perovskites are promising candidates for solar cells. However, the processing strategies that promote large, oriented grains often concurrently induce tensile strain and microcracks, creating a critical growth‐strain trade‐off. Herein, we propose a surface self‐templated dual‐anion synergy by partially substituting iodide with low amounts of thiocyanate and chloride (2 mol%) in 2D (AA)2(MA)3Pb4I13 perovskites (n = 4), in which SCN anion spontaneously enriches at the top surface as a structure‐directing template that drives oriented grain growth but inevitably introduces tensile strain, and Cl anion concurrently segregates to the top surface as a strain buffer that alleviates this strain without sacrificing grain size. Systematic in situ and depth‐resolved analysis reveals that such synergy effectively navigates the growth‐strain trade‐off of 2D perovskites, yielding enlarged grains, strong vertical orientation, and a crack‐free morphology, which contributes to the suppression of non‐radiative recombination and the enhancement of charge transport in solar cells. As a result, the champion device with dual‐anion engineering achieves a remarkable efficiency of 19.11%, and retains over 95% of its initial efficiency after 1800 h under one‐sun irradiation. This work establishes a fundamental understanding of the growth‐strain dilemma in 2D perovskites, providing a universal design principle for high‐efficiency 2D perovskite solar cells.
neb0cfcb16535: The exploration of energy-efficient and functional spintronics has attracted considerable attention. Spin-orbit and orbital transport have opened new pathways for current-induced torque generation based on the spin Hall effect. In addition, artificial intelligence computing has been demonstrated using spintronic devices. Further progress of these devices can be anticipated through the development of unique and functional materials, beyond the existing heavy metals and topological systems with strong spin–orbit coupling. The nitride materials exhibit unique chemical, magnetic, and structural versatility, including antiferromagnetism, high thermal stability, and compatibility with diverse device architectures. Here, we propose Nitrospinics as a conceptual and functional framework that exploits nitride materials for applications ranging from spin-orbit and orbital torque based spintronic devices to artificial intelligence hardware. Using a sputter-grown multilayer Cr2N with MXene-related layer structure and a nitrogen-incorporated heavy metal of Pt x N, as prototype systems, we discuss how nitrogen contributes to the structural stability, the orbital torque and spin-orbit torque generation, and the interfacial orbital to spin conversion. We further outline key challenges and opportunities toward establishing nitride-based materials for next-generation computing technologies.
n64966edb3342: Topological materials represent unique solids characterized by the global invariance of their bulk electronic band structure. Owing to their distinctive properties, such as ultra‐high electron mobility, spin‐momentum locking, and the presence of massless Dirac fermions, topological materials provide a promising platform for applications in electronics, spintronics, and energy conversion. By integrating topological materials with other functional systems, it is possible to harness the advantages of topologically protected surface states along with other versatile properties, thereby enabling novel optical behaviors for photo‐driven applications. In this review, we provide a concise overview of recent advances in the rational design and optical responses of topological and plasmonic heterostructures, emphasizing their unique advantages and potential in photothermal and photocatalytic applications. We begin by examining the fundamental principles and optical characteristics of topological materials, as well as the underlying mechanisms responsible for their enhanced photothermal and catalytic performance. Subsequently, we review recent progress in the chemical and physical preparation of both two‐component and three‐component topological–plasmonic heterostructures, along with their resulting optical responses. Finally, we highlight significant recent developments in the use of topological and plasmonic heterostructures for photothermal and photocatalytic applications and offer a brief perspective on current challenges and future research directions.
n0d1bec6f410e: The discovery of efficient, durable, and platinum group metal‐free electrocatalysts for alkaline water electrolysis is essential to reduce the cost of green hydrogen. Efficient exploration of the vast possible synthetic space is nevertheless hindered by the slow pace of manual experimentation. Here, a closed‐loop optimization is presented that combines an automated electrocatalyst synthesis and testing system, CatBot, with Bayesian optimization and accelerated stress testing at industrial conditions for the rapid discovery of active and durable NiMo coatings. Distinct regions with exceptionally high activity and stability are identified within limited experimental budgets on a nickel wire substrate, using different search strategies to efficiently navigate the six‐dimensional synthesis space exceeding 1014$10^{14}$ possible combinations. The most promising coatings are upscaled onto technological nickel foam electrodes showing platinum‐level catalytic activity with overpotentials of 173 mV at –1Acm−2${\;\rm Acm}^{-2}$ in 30 wt.% KOH at 80∘C$80^{\circ }{\rm C}$ for the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the autonomous optimization of functional electrocatalyst coatings under realistic operating conditions.
nd036c493be08: Early detection and intervention are critical to reducing colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality. Although tumor‐derived exosomes (TDEs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, their extremely low abundance in peripheral blood during early carcinogenesis severely limits clinical utility for early diagnosis. Here, we report a theranostic magnetic nanorobot (MNP‐BC), comprising Fe3O4@SiO2 nanoparticles co‐functionalized with butyrate and anti‐CD147 antibody. Oral administration followed by magnetic guidance, MNP‐BC accumulates at colonic tumor sites, where butyrate selectively induces cancer cell apoptosis, boosts CD8+ T‐cell cytotoxicity, and preserves intestinal barrier integrity. Concurrently, the anti‐CD147 antibody moiety captures TDEs in situ. Following monocarboxylate transporter–mediated uptake, intracellular butyrate metabolism releases the MNP–TDEs complex into circulation, thereby enriching plasma TDEs for magnetic isolation and noninvasive detection. In early‐stage CRC mice, MNP‐BC markedly suppressed tumor progression and facilitated sensitive diagnosis via TDEs signal amplification. This work introduces an integrated “TDEs signal amplification–sensitive diagnosis–in situ therapy” platform, offering a rationally engineered strategy to address key translational barriers in early CRC detection and intervention.
n783c0b2acf7b: Tailoring phase purity in 2D/3D perovskites is essential for balanced charge transport and long‐term stability. Here, we develop a nanocrystal‐templated epitaxial strategy to construct phase‐pure 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions. Phase‐pure 2D perovskite nanocrystals with tunable quantum‐well thickness (n = 1–4) are used as templates to direct lattice‐matched epitaxial growth of 3D perovskites, yielding coherent 2D/3D interfaces. By precisely controlling the 2D quantum‐well thickness, we eliminate the phase‐mixing issues of conventional methods and ensure high interfacial phase purity. A series of well‐defined 2D/3D heterojunctions (n = 1–4) exhibits balanced charge transport and markedly reduced recombination losses. The optimized 2D (n = 4)/3D perovskite solar cell delivers a power conversion efficiency of 26.48% and retains over 90% of its initial performance after 1 600 h, demonstrating enhanced efficiency and long‐term stability. Our work provides a versatile route for constructing phase‐pure 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions, enabling optoelectronic devices with balanced charge transport and long‐term stability.
n547e66b762d2: Non‐fused ring electron acceptors (NFREAs) provide a low‐cost alternative to fused‐ring electron acceptors for organic solar cells (OSCs). Nevertheless, how terminal substituents on alkyl side chains modulate the crystallization behavior of NFREAs remains largely underexplored. Herein, two NFREAs, namely TTF‐F (fluorine‐terminated side chains) and TTO‐F (methoxy‐terminated side chains), were constructed with identical intramolecular conformational locks and terminal IC acceptor units. Although the two molecules possess nearly identical electronic structures, in situ UV–vis absorption spectroscopy confirms that TTF‐F exhibits much faster crystallization kinetics (completing aggregation within 206 ms) relative to TTO‐F (336 ms). Femtosecond transient absorption measurements demonstrate that the hole‐transfer process in D18:TTF‐F blends proceeds fourfold more rapidly (τ1 = 0.26 ps) than that in D18:TTO‐F (τ1 = 1.14 ps), consistent with the more ordered π–π stacking revealed by grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS). When paired with the polymer donor D18, TTF‐F delivers an outstanding power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.02%, far exceeding the 13.35% efficiency of TTO‐F‐based devices. This substantial performance discrepancy mainly stems from distinct crystallization dynamics and resultant thin‐film microstructures. This work establishes a structure–kinetics–morphology–performance relationship for NFREAs by tuning side‐chain terminal groups and offers rational molecular design strategies to fabricate high‐efficiency NFREA‐based OSCs.
ndad3b9f30b97: Current therapies for chronic infected wounds primarily rely on multifunctional nanoplatforms with antibacterial, anti‐biofilm, and anti‐inflammatory properties. However, biofilms are often overlooked as the initial physical barrier that must be disrupted before therapeutic agents can effectively penetrate deep inflammatory tissues and eliminate residual infection. In addition, heterogeneous infection microenvironments demand versatile therapeutic systems. To address these challenges, this study developed self‐propelled nanomotors (Dex@CQDs@mPDA) and proposed a spatially progressive penetration strategy to achieve precise, stepwise treatment from the surface to deep tissues. First, dextran (Dex) surface modification enables targeted recognition of bacterial biofilms, while the near‐infrared (NIR) photothermal effect facilitates biofilm disruption. Subsequently, mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA) catalyzes H2O2 to generate O2, which, together with carbon quantum dots (CQDs)‐mediated NO release, produces a dual‐gas‐driven propulsion effect, promoting active penetration into deep inflammatory tissues. Meanwhile, the nanomotors effectively scavenge excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), promote macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, enhance angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and remodel the inflammatory microenvironment to accelerate tissue regeneration. In vitro experiments further confirmed their excellent antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anti‐inflammatory activities, as well as their broad applicability across diverse infection scenarios. This work provides a therapeutic strategy that links biofilm eradication with deep inflammation resolution.
n66abfec6c4c8: Hierarchical control of molecular transport requires not only multiple regulatory inputs, but also a relationship in which an initial structural feature influences how a subsequent stimulus modifies the transport response. Here, we investigate this concept using two azulene‐based molecular wires that share the same conjugated core and thioether anchor chemistry but differ in the position of one terminal anchoring group on an ancillary phenyl ring. Electrochemically gated scanning tunneling microscope break junction measurements were used to map their conductance‐potential characteristics over the same potential window in both the neutral and protonated states. This matched four‐state comparison reveals opposite monotonic conductance responses for the neutral para‐ and meta‐linked junctions. Upon protonation, the para derivative develops a peak‐shaped anti‐ambipolar characteristic, whereas the meta derivative exhibits a valley‐shaped ambipolar response. These distinct changes indicate that protonation does not modify the two junctions uniformly, but instead produces transfer characteristics that depend on the pre‐existing anchoring topology. Our findings suggest that molecular topology can be used not only to tune an initial transport state, but also to shape its response to a subsequent chemical input, offering a strategy for constructing molecular junctions with differentiated gate‐response functions.
n51ecd6020146: The key challenge for advancing next‐generation mechanical metamaterials lies in systematically discovering and harnessing the beneficial nonlinear mechanical characteristics. This work introduces a novel class of mechanical metamaterials exhibiting morphological nonlinearity of mechanics in stiffness and Poisson's ratio, achieving purposeful nonlinear performance with quasi‐zero stiffness (QZS) through topological transformations from X‐shaped rigid‐body mechanism. The proposed topology transformation miniaturizes, reshapes, and reprograms tailorable nonlinear stiffness of solid mechanism into elastic metamaterial. Governed by compliant elements and nonlinear meta‐atoms, architected matrices culminate in a novel family termed as X‐QZS metamaterial. Localized topology faithfully emulates the nonlinear kinematics of their rigid‐body counterparts, meanwhile meta‐atoms incubate tailorable nonlinear stiffness with topological morphologies. Assembled in nonlinear Poisson's ratio matrix, X‐QZS matrix reprograms nonlinear stiffness from meta‐atomic level into stabilized structural pattern. Experimental demonstrations validate the presence of QZS in multiple configurations as analytically determined in the topology design, achieving wide‐bandwidth vibration isolation starting from 2 Hz and attenuating vibration energy from external sources by more than 98%. X‐QZS metamaterial with tailorable dual nonlinearity and its topology pave the way of developing functional mechanical metamaterials transferred from rigid‐body structures, which reprogram and reshape large‐scale mechanisms into continuum deformable metamaterial of equivalent performance.
nbf8206fc37d6: Oral tumors are not shaped by biochemical signals alone; they also evolve within mechanically active and thermally fluctuating microenvironments that critically regulate malignant progression, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance. Here, we develop a dynamic bioorthogonal organoid platform that couples a 3D‐printed photothermal elastic scaffold with an interpenetrating hydrogel network derived from decellularized oral mucosa extracellular matrix, enabling the reconstruction of in vivo‐like structural support, matrix‐derived biochemical cues, spatial cellular compartmentalization, and dynamic physical stimulation. Through click chemistry‐mediated cell anchorage and hydrogel encapsulation, oral cancer cells and macrophages are spatially organized into a compartmentalized cancer–immune niche. Under cyclic mechanical stretch and near‐infrared‐triggered periodic photothermal stimulation, dynamic culture markedly enhances cancer cell proliferation and glycolytic reprogramming while concomitantly polarizing macrophages toward a pro‐tumoral M2 phenotype. In both monoculture and coculture settings, biochemical–mechano–thermal stimulation substantially increases cancer cell chemoresistance. Mechanistically, these biochemical‐physical cues activate stress‐adaptive and survival programs while enriching cancer stem‐like populations. In a xenograft mouse model exposed to in vivo biochemical, mechanical and thermal stimulation, dynamic conditioning markedly accelerates tumor progression, enhances metastatic potential, and confers pronounced chemoresistance. Together, this study establishes a biomimetic multicellular tumor platform for uncovering how dynamic biochemical‐physical cues orchestrate cancer–immune crosstalk and therapeutic failure.
n2935b2c8bf8e: Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal‐oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi‐n‐i‐p active layer comprising an acceptor‐rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor‐rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes cascade energy‐level alignment and preserves interfacial integrity, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction and suppressing recombination losses. As a result, the optimal device achieves a PCE of 20.58%, with a certified efficiency of 20.07%, placing it among the highest reported for single‐junction inverted OSCs. This architecture was successfully fabricated with different donor‐rich layers, BHJ cores, and acceptor‐rich layers, demonstrating broader material applicability across multiple material combinations. Interfacial adhesion and vertical compositional control improve electrical continuity, enhance charge generation and transport, and reduce trap‐assisted and bimolecular recombination, leading to higher open‐circuit voltage, short‐circuit current density, and fill factor. This work provides a scalable route to active‐layer engineering in inverted OSCs and offers a general strategy for high‐performance organic photovoltaic fabrication.
ne6d9bc053562: Dimer acceptors are attractive for organic solar cells (OSCs) owing to their combination of stability and high efficiency, yet the efficiency of dimer‐based binary devices has long stagnated below 20%. The limitation stems from weak intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and poor locally excited/charge‐transfer (LE/CT) state hybridization, which are direct consequences of the canceled dipole moments in symmetric dimer architectures. In this work, we adopt an asymmetric‐isomerization strategy to design two novel dual‐asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl‐YF and QF‐YCl. Compared with QCl‐YF, QF‐YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron‐hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Moreover, the stronger electrostatic potential and dipole moment of QF‐YCl enhances the intermolecular interactions to improve donor/acceptor compatibility and film‐forming process in blend film, consequently leading to more ordered film morphology. Consequently, the QF‐YCl‐based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl‐YF), achieving the highest efficiency for dimer‐based binary OSCs. This work demonstrates that asymmetric‐isomerization is a precise and effective design strategy for high‐performance dimer acceptors.
n9ab08a197d82: The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. Herein, we report a dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA2EA2Pb3Br10 (1, where BA is n‐butylamine and EA is ethylamine) ferroelectric single‐crystalline thin‐films (SCFs). The 1 ferroelectric SCFs show a photoresponsivity that reaches 230% of the original level under +1.13% tensile strain. Notably, we innovatively define the strain‐ratio key (ε1/ε2, ε2/ε3, ε3/ε4) induced by distinct bending states as the intrinsic unclonable hardware secret key, and construct a 4‐bit combined coding scheme based on four distinguishable photocurrent levels modulated by these strain ratios to realize secure transmission of the message “FJIRSM.” This strain ratio‐based system avoids complex optical modulation, ensuring ultrahigh security, and expands the application of two‐dimensional ferroelectrics in advanced encrypted optoelectronics.
nca77360e8365: Cation pre‐intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn2+ storage capacity has been adequately studied, an in‐depth understanding of the influence of intercalants on proton storage is still lacking. Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre‐intercalated K+ in K0.5V6O13 (KVO) not only reinforces the [VO] framework but also optimizes the hydrogen‐bonded network composed of confined lattice water, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO improve significantly. KVO delivers a high reversible capacity of 462.9 mAh g−1 at 0.2 A g−1 and 82.3% retention after 20000 cycles at 20 A g−1. Even with the high mass loading of 19.2 mg cm−2, a KVO||Zn pouch cell with 539.2 mAh capacity can achieve stable cycling for more than 300 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. This work provides new insights into how pre‐intercalated cations affect the proton topochemistry and electrochemical performance of inorganic cathodes.
n633da7e32909: The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) for H2O2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O2 activation and H2O2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO2. The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H2O2‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H2O2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h−1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.
n260c772b9fc8: Strain engineering offers a powerful means to regulate the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of active metal sites, yet a general framework linking strain to electrocatalytic performance remains elusive beyond the conventional d‐band model. Here we report crumpled double‐transition‐metal MXene nanosheets (Mo2TiC2Tx) decorated with Pt single atoms, in which a tunable strain field is introduced through a physical diaphragm balloon method. The resulting cMo2TiC2Tx‐PtSA catalyst exhibits outstanding alkaline hydrogen evolution performance, requiring overpotentials of only 24.9 and 75.5 mV to reach 10 and 50 mA cm−2, respectively, together with a mass activity of 11 859 mA mgPt−1, around 178‐fold higher than commercial Pt/C, a Tafel slope of 31.61 mV dec−1 and excellent durability. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that the ordered long‐range strain field around isolated Pt sites accelerates interfacial water activation while preserving near‐optimal H adsorption, thereby facilitating H2 release. The resulting catalyst delivered a high current density of 3 A cm−2 at a low voltage of 1.98 V and maintained stable operation at 1000 mA cm−2 for over 500 h. These performance metrics underscore the potential of cMo2TiC2Tx‐PtSA for industrial applications.
nf329f7915b9b: Anti‐counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time‐resolved physically unclonable function (TR‐PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high‐dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron‐based room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent‐free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram‐level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color‐tunable emission. The formation of rigid B‐O‐C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels–an essential prerequisite for high‐entropy time‐resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi‐emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual‐entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time‐gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine‐learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time‐gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.
n1b669f58780b: Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li+ sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li+ solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6Li/7Li isotope tracing identify Li2SO4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m−2. This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.
ncf574fda2631: Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z‐scheme CuWO4/poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites for CO2‐to‐ethanol conversion. Site‐selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge‐asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z‐scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g−1 h−1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the *CO─*CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.
nb435aa966562: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O2‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO2+) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.
nc849f363f339: Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.
nf1d867eafa59: All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization‐induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π‐donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC)2Ge][OTf]2 (4), the first two‐coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c‐4e C‐Ge‐C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge‐centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1‐oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge‐donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8, featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three‐center two‐electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC‐based low‐coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main‐group dications.
n63e4c6aae79d: Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H2O2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce3+/Ce4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.
n007432bcf39f: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp2‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H2O2 selectivity, and improved 2e− ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H2O2 production rate of 27.8 mol g−1 h−1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.
