n727bf8b39f97: Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na0.44MnO2, where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na0.44MnO2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.
n2e3151f70e74: GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410, the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410, maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.
n12a7c6c63bd2: Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al2O3 to inverse Al2O3/Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double-volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al2O3 and inverse Al2O3/90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al2O3/90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space-time yield of 65 mmol gcat −1 h−1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial-rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction-order measurements, apparent activation-energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double-volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition-dependent balance between Lewis-acid-assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen-dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen-dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al2O3 than over Al2O3/90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non-noble-metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.
n4422e6412ac0: To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g−1 h−1, marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.
n3e8646b7dff4: Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.
n76e78cf545f1: The efficient hydrogenation of CO2 to light olefins over Fe-based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long-overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low-concentration guar gum, hydrogen-bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter-free Fe achieves a CO2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra-high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL gcat −1 h−1. Meanwhile, the space-time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kgcat −1 h−1, which outperforms all of the reported Fe-based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.
n14369a705616: Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni2+ and Co2+, affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO2/CO electroreduction to CH4. This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.
nfcc4e8ace503: Coupling electrochemical CO2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO2 into value‐added products. We present proof‐of‐concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L−1. While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.
ncc79e8b17bd3: p-Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed-valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5]2 +•[FeCl4]− (OR5-MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl3. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation-radical dimer [OR5]2 +•, acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5]4 2+ tetramer via a multi-center–two-electron bond, which further aggregates into a one-dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open-shell singlet ground state for [OR5]4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake-bond formation between OR5 cation-radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one-dimensional columnar architecture of OR5-MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10− 3 S cm− 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10− 9 S cm− 1), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.
n07777580afdf: The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower‐energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near‐infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low‐energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.
n9c04f195a7c8: Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O2 and H2O2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.
nd88cde2749f5: Hybrid organic-inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site-specific control over their high-pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero-dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm)6[MnCl4∙MnCl6] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl6]4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl4]2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure-sensitive red emission as a probe, a self-calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high-pressure x-ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl6]4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl4]2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic-inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self-calibrated optical sensing materials for next-generation metrology.
n18475b3f44b5: Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates (k RISC) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation-caused quenching and significant efficiency roll-off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy-atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC, and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof-of-concept emitters BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN-FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 106 s−1, maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non-sensitized OLEDs based on BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show pure-green electroluminescence with CIEy coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmaxs) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m−2, respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQEmaxs of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.
nc7d5197ad5a0: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well-defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular-level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage-angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o-TPDA-COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o-TPDA-COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o-TPDA-COF reaches an excellent H2O2 productivity of 12.82 mol gcat −1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e– oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.
n318b3a927aa9: A supported NiGa alloy promoted the RWGS reaction via a hydrogen-assisted CO 2 reduction mechanism, achieving 36.5% CO 2 conversion with 95.2% CO selectivity.
n6f9cb1bf74cb: The one-pot conversion of concentrated glucose solutions to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) is highly sought after by industries; however, due to poor selectivity, product instability and difficult isolation, it remains a challenge....
nf8412247aa79: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.
neaeb3c1505d4: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.
nd38b8af0450d: Applicability and uncertainties of the BET analysis for porous materials, and its emerging alternatives.
n6590c73a60cf: Prussian blue analogues AxM[Fe(CN)6]1–y·zH2O (A = Na, K, M = Fe, Mn) possess a rich crystal chemistry that allows their use as insertion materials for batteries, water treatment, and smart windows, among others, applications. Despite being simple in appearance, their synthesis is complex and often results in defective, nonstoichiometric materials. These defects can be of neutral charge, such as interstitial water molecules, or charged, such as A+ vacancies or [Fe(CN)6]n− vacancies, whose presence implies charge balance by the remaining transition metal centers. In this work, a compound close to the Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN)6] nominal composition was synthesized, and its crystal structure, electrochemical properties, and electronic structure were investigated. Although usual characterization methods such as X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy agree well with the formation of Fe[Fe(CN)6], the material can only be intercalated to Na1.4Fe[Fe(CN)6]. This lack of capacity was hypothesized to arise from “hidden” [Fe(CN)6] vacancies. The charge balance associated with these vacancies implies partial reduction of the low-spin Fe, as confirmed by low-temperature 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and further high-angular-resolution diffraction experiments. This study suggests that numerous materials previously described as “Berlin green” in the literature might actually be substantially hexacyanoferrate defective.
nfecfae089ada: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) fundamentally relies on a distinct disparity in surface chemical states between growth and nongrowth area. For SiO2/Cu patterned architectures, the oxidation of the Cu surface serves as a primary driver for the loss of selectivity as the ALD process proceeds. Herein, an alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is proposed, utilizing alcohols with varying carbon chain lengths to precisely modulate surface chemical states to enhance selectivity of AS-ALD WOx film. A competitive-synergistic mechanism involving surface reductive capability and steric hindrance is identified as the governing factor for process selectivity. Results demonstrate that while the reducing ability of alcohols on oxidized Cu surfaces diminishes with increasing carbon chain length, their steric hindrance increases. EtOH was identified as the optimal pretreatment agent, yielding an exceptional selectivity exceeding 99.9% on SiO2/Cu patterned surface. Moreover, the alcohol-mediated AS-ALD process is successfully extended to other oxide systems with precursors bearing analogous ligands, demonstrating the generality of the proposed strategy. This work provides a versatile methodology for modulating surface reductive capability and steric hindrance to achieve high-selectivity AS-ALD.
n4b6cc05951ad: Colloidal germanium quantum dots (GeQDs) hold promise for solution-processable optoelectronics, yet their performance is often constrained by the limited reactivity of hydride-terminated surfaces and the insulating nature of conventional capping ligands. Here, we introduce a room-temperature selenylation strategy that harnesses the intrinsically weak and polarizable Ge–H bonds on freshly etched GeQD surfaces to drive Se–Se bond activation of diorganyl diselenides. This polarization-assisted concerted process proceeds without radical initiators or external stimuli, yielding robust Ge–SeR surface linkages that effectively passivate the GeQDs against oxidation while introducing a soft, polarizable chalcogenide-rich surface. The resulting RSe-GeQDs show notably improved optical properties and charge carrier mobilities compared to oleylamine-functionalized GeQDs. The direct, catalyst-free nature of this approach offers a versatile platform for the development of solution-processable germanium-based optoelectronic devices.
n9a6ea7e8b76f: Electrolytes composed of mixed solvents are of significant scientific and technological importance in lithium-ion and beyond-lithium-ion batteries, and more broadly across physical chemistry. Their emergence has highlighted the importance of multiscale phenomena, particularly the development of nanoscale solution heterogeneities. It is therefore essential to assess how these inhomogeneities and nanoscale aggregates influence solvation, transport, and electronic properties. Here we investigate the solution structure and transport properties of aqueous zinc sulfate electrolytes with acetonitrile (ACN) additives, where the addition of ACN leads to improved cyclability. Using complementary anomalous small-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray pair distribution function, electrochemistry, and NMR, we identify the presence of salt-rich-water-rich and salt-poor-ACN-rich nanoheterogeneities and, at higher ACN concentrations, liquid–liquid phase separation. We find that the size of zinc sulfate ion clusters in the water domains increases slightly upon ACN addition, while the ACN-rich domains grow much larger as phase separation is approached. The inverse Haven ratio, determined using the ionic conductivity and diffusivity, is much less than unity and decreases slightly upon addition of ACN, which shows ion–ion interactions. We speculate that the increased ion–ion interactions with increased ACN are a result of a reduction in free water, the increase in zinc sulfate cluster size, and/or an increase in solution tortuosity. This work highlights key phenomena to consider when engineering new water-organic-salt electrolyte systems and establishes a phase diagram for water–ACN–ZnSO4 that can guide advances, such as self-adaptive electrolytes.

n9bf97f69680b: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. n24a7fb176953: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. n4ba15a4909b2: Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical stimuli into chemical energy, holds significant promise for noninvasive medical therapies. In this process, ultrasonic frequency plays a dual role: it governs both the reaction rate and the electromechanical coupling efficiency, thereby serving as a critical bridge between microscopic and macroscopic physical processes. However, conventional theoretical models lack a multiscale description of coupled physical processes and thus fail to reveal how frequency dictates catalytic activity. Here, we develop an integrated multiscale framework that links, for the first time, macroscopic bubble cavitation dynamics, mesoscopic piezoelectric constitutive relations, and microscopic chemical reaction rate─with ultrasonic frequency as the unifying thread. Our model uncovers the complete frequency-dependent activity profile and elucidates the physical origin of an optimal frequency, predicting a volcano-shaped activity-frequency relationship that agrees well with a range of experimental reports. By reinterpreting piezocatalysis from a multiscale physical field perspective, this work establishes a new theoretical paradigm for the rational design of piezocatalysts.
naa950e007946: Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.
nb918909d59a3: The frameworks of zeolite molecular sieves constructed from a sole type of ring, such as 6-membered rings (6MRs), are regarded as unachievable structures that would not even be found in hypothetical zeolite databases containing tens of millions of structures. Herein, we for the first time report a novel aluminophosphate ZJM-11 molecular sieve, with a fully 6-membered ring (6MR) framework, which was successfully obtained from topotactic transformation. The obtained structure, which possesses fully opened micropores, represents a rare case of a single-ring zeolite topology with an ultrahigh framework density, viewed from the perspective of conventional wisdom as an “unachievable” molecular sieve. Advanced characterizations unveil the dynamic framework reconstruction mediated by ZJM-9 and/or ZJM-10 intermediates, pinpointing this structural evolution as the essential step toward ZJM-11 formation. This work therefore delivers critical knowledge for the rational design of unconventional zeolite molecular sieves.
n6f6f97c10479: Chemical methods are promising avenues to recycle fiber-reinforced polymer waste. Here, we reintroduce tripotassium phosphate-mediated benzyl alcohol conditions for epoxy cleavage. While these conditions were developed in 2008 for anhydride-cured epoxy cleavage and have been applied to amine-linked epoxy cleavage, no account has been made of why these conditions should work with the latter, or why air exposure appears critical for their success. We now show how benzaldehyde, formed in situ from benzyl alcohol, plays the crucial redox role that enables selective C–N bond cleavage: tertiary amines are cleaved by a previously uncharacterized mechanism in which benzaldehyde facilitates iminium formation from the polymer’s C–N linkage. Subsequent hydrolysis and base-promoted elimination cleave the C═N and C–O bonds, respectively, enabling the recovery of bisphenol A and release of the linking diamines. Carbon fiber (CF) and even glass fiber (GF) fabrics are preserved, and recovered CF fabrics are remanufactured into second-generation composites with near-virgin quality and mechanical performance. These mechanistic insights may inform the future development of selective diamine recovery strategies from thermosets, which is a challenge when valorizing composites. Collectively, these results present promising recycling conditions with the potential to valorize matrices and fibers from a wide range of composites, spanning high-performance carbon fiber to widely used fiberglass.
n140416ba1b3d: Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC–photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay. The Z-scheme heterostructure of a plasmonic Au nanoparticle (NP) layer-supported BiOI/AgI/indium tin oxide glass (BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO) is constructed as the initial photoelectrode. In the sensing process, a CEA recognition event directly reshapes the phase composition of BiOI/AgI, charge-transfer behavior, and photoresponse polarity. The synergistic integration of the BiOI/AgI heterostructure and the close-packed layer of plasmonic Au NPs substantially enhance the light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial charge transfer, making BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO a highly suitable photoelectrode for the PEC mode of the PEC–PT biosensor. This analyte-driven phase evolution reconstructs the semiconductor composition, band alignment, and charge-transfer pathways to switch the photocurrent polarity from cathodic to anodic. In addition, a photothermal imaging mode of the PEC–PT biosensor is triggered by regulating the Bi2S3 formation for intrinsic cross-validation. By integrating an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted analysis, PEC–PT biosensors enable robust multimodal quantification and improved analytical reliability, achieving > 99.8% prediction accuracy in real-sample analysis. This is the first example of integrating a dynamic nanointerface-driven PEC–PT dual-mode biosensor with artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced multimodal analysis for CEA detection and provides a dynamic nanointerface-driven strategy for intelligent multimode biosensing.
n2e912b852bc6: Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.
n6f6463e29115: Lattice-oxygen-mediated pathways bypass the energy-intensive steps that constrain adsorbate-mediated catalysis. Activating these pathways under mild conditions, however, means breaking metal–oxygen bonds that are, by design, strong. Asymmetric M1-O-M2 motifs, in which a bridging oxygen sits between two cations of different electronic character, decouple oxygen activation from oxygen release by distributing these functions across chemically distinct sites. Here, we show that a Cu-doped In2O3 system with a well-defined asymmetric Cu–O–In unit exhibits enhanced photoinduced lattice oxygen activity. Series (quasi) in situ spectroscopy captures the activation, consumption, and replenishment of lattice oxygen under illumination in real time. Photogenerated carriers populate around the Cu–O site preferentially, weakening the Cu–O bond enough to extract lattice oxygen at room temperature. The optimized material, Cui-In2O3, gives a response of 32.4 toward 5 ppm of H2S under visible light. The results connect local coordination asymmetry directly to photoinduced oxygen functionality and suggest a route toward photodriven catalysts built around asymmetric oxygen sites.
n39479dc994e2: Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton-exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl– + CH3Cl), and proton-transfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O···H+···OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware/noise-models show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware. These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.
n0177c343b6b1: Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.
n553395a44679: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.
ne8280113fc39: Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.
n99c8d1d82891: Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) solids derived from MXenes exhibit attractive physical and chemical properties but are usually limited by the irreversible phase transformation of MXenes into rocksalt structures at high temperatures. Herein, we develop a vapor-phase chemical intercalation strategy mediated by high-vapor-pressure zinc (Zn) to efficiently stabilize the transition metals (Ti, Nb, and V) with unsaturated d-orbitals in MXenes. This stabilization facilitates subsequent interlayer bonding via reaction with various metal vapors (Al, Ga, and In) at elevated temperatures, yielding a family of well-defined non-vdW solids with ultrathin layered structures. Moreover, this strategy is readily scalable, enabling the fabrication of a continuous non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film featuring a heterogeneous architecture with a reconstructed MAX-like bonded region and a locally unbonded MXene region. These structural features endow the non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film with exceptional mechanical flexibility, high-temperature oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air, and an electrical conductivity of ∼10 000 S cm–1. Consequently, the film demonstrates an electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness of up to 47.9 dB at a thickness of 5 μm, along with durable infrared stealth performance under prolonged exposure at 500 °C for 48 h.
ne7f7662e54a4: Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.
n5f9dcee2f6bc: Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we first report an inorganic inter-reinforced organic composite separator, fabricated by pairing cellulose with a zinc oxide (ZnO)-enhanced layer and designed to regulate the electrolyte solvation architecture by effectively anchoring solvent molecules. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that the electron-deficient Zn sites on ZnO enhance the solvent-capture ability of the polar hydroxyl groups on cellulose via bidirectional charge transfer. This interaction reconfigures the Mg2+ solvation sheath into a unique single-cluster structure, steering the formation of a dense, ultrathin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that facilitates rapid Mg2+ desolvation while suppressing parasitic side reactions. Consequently, the as-assembled Mg||Mg symmetric cells deliver an exceptional cycling lifespan exceeding 2000 h with minimal overpotential and exhibit robust compatibility across diverse electrolyte systems. This inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy for modulating solvation chemistry offers a generalizable avenue toward long-life and high-safety magnesium metal batteries.
n55245281bfda: We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to < 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.
nd4c00d19279c: Deterministic spin–orbit torque (SOT) switching of perpendicular magnets without external magnetic fields remains a central challenge for scalable SOT-MRAM. Here, we demonstrate that dimensional engineering of a Co/W superlattice spin–orbit layer enables >90% field-free switching of perpendicular CoFeB. Harmonic Hall measurements reveal an unconventional out-of-plane torque, while first-principles calculations reveal reconstruction of the spin-resolved electronic structure and increased W-projected out-of-plane spin character, together supporting the modification of torque symmetry through Co/W superlattice engineering. The optimized superlattice achieves a critical current density of 23.3 MA cm–2 and a thermal stability factor Δ ≈ 45. Nanoscale devices (100 nm) preserve deterministic field-free reversal with comparable efficiency, confirming scalability toward magnetic tunnel junction integration. Micromagnetic analysis shows that out-of-plane spin-polarized torque together with canted anisotropy enables intrinsic symmetry breaking, highlighting superlattice engineering as a route to tailor torque symmetry for effective field-free SOT devices.
n3fa7a23451ce: Electronic phases in quantum materials are often governed by nanoscale inhomogeneity, where local order develops within spatially confined regions, or puddles. A prominent example is an incommensurate charge-density-wave (I-CDW) comprising locally commensurate domains. In 2H-NbSe2, such an I-CDW state persists alongside lattice anharmonicity and superconductivity, raising fundamental questions about the dynamical stabilization of CDW order in puddles. Here, using Raman scattering, we reveal a strong Fano-coupling between interlayer shear phonons and the CDW amplitude mode. Our time-resolved reflectivity measurement shows a low-frequency ∼0.2 THz coherent overdamped oscillation onsetting within the CDW regime at ∼17K, indicating a previously unexplored transition. This we identify as a Fano-coupled phonon-CDW hybrid emerging from the collective dynamics of CDW puddles. We establish an overdamped-oscillator framework for capturing such intertwined glassy dynamics. These results highlight how lattice pinning and electronic correlations shape CDW order in layered materials, insight crucial for designing novel van der Waals devices.
n6eea938e73a1: Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs) require encapsulation to extend their storage and operational lifetime. However, acidic encapsulants commonly used usually induce an anomalous positive aging phenomenon─the device performance improves rather than decreases in the initial days. These uncontrollable gains hinder the commercialization of QD-LEDs, yet no study to date has directly probed the in situ evolution of charge carriers during this process. Here, we employ electrically excited transient absorption (EETA) spectroscopy to investigate how encapsulants influence charge carrier dynamics in QD-LEDs. Taking red QD-LEDs as a model system, we demonstrate that positive aging is accompanied by enhanced electron charging in the quantum dot (QD) layer and accelerated electron injection into the emissive layer. Furthermore, we show that acid-induced progressive passivation of surface defects on ZnMgO nanoparticles improves electron injection efficiency. This work reveals that enhanced electron charging induces positive aging in QD-LEDs.
n5a254d60c0c3: Dual emissive materials are of particular importance in chemical and biological assays. Herein, we focus on a rod-shaped Au42(SCH2CH2Ph)32 nanocluster that exhibits dual emission at 875 and 1040 nm owing to fluorescence (FL) and phosphorescence (PH), respectively. Transient absorption analysis shows a slow intersystem crossing (ISC, ∼500 ps) from lowest singlet S1 to triplet T1 upon direct S1 excitation, leading to dual emission from both S1 and T1. However, upon excitation of the higher Sn state, we observe a metastable singlet state (S′). We rationalize two competing decay pathways from S′: (i) internal conversion to S1 and (ii) ISC to high triplet Tn≥2. These processes alter the populations of the S1 and T1 states, which explains the excitation-wavelength-dependent dual emission and FL/PH ratios. The revealed excited-state mechanism and the dual emissive Au42 material will serve as a paradigm for future research on atomically precise nanoclusters.
n866eeec6f551: Chemically and structurally diverse two-dimensional semiconductors exhibit a broad range of excitonic and optical phenomena that have direct implications for optoelectronic functionality. We examine these materials from a first-principles many-body perspective, emphasizing the connection between microscopic excitonic structure and optoelectronic functionality. Reduced symmetry and orbital character produce polarization-selective absorption, while dimensionality, dielectric screening, and exciton fine structure govern binding energies and radiative behavior. In layered systems, interlayer electrostatics and type-II band alignment promote charge separation, whereas exciton–phonon coupling activates indirect optical transitions and shapes temperature-dependent spectra. These mechanisms establish common design principles for excitonic engineering, whereby the dielectric environment, crystal geometry, lattice dynamics, and stacking are used to control exciton properties and tailor optical functionality. This perspective moves beyond description toward the ab initio prediction and design of emerging 2D materials for targeted optoelectronic applications, including polarization-sensitive photodetection and ultrathin solar-energy conversion.
n6c7461761eac: Fast-charging lithium-ion batteries require cathodes that sustain rapid Li+ transport while maintaining structural and interfacial stability. Here, we investigate particle-size effects in γ-MnO2 by comparing micron-sized (4.4 ± 0.8 μm) and nanosized (62 ± 21 nm) particles under identical conditions. Nanosized γ-MnO2 delivers 160.1 mAh g–1 at C/10 and retains ∼66% capacity at 5C while exhibiting lower charge-transfer and diffusion-related impedance. Cyclic voltammetry and Dunn’s analysis reveal a 68.9% capacitive contribution at 2 mV s–1, indicating a shift toward faster surface-controlled charge storage enabled by increased surface area and shorter Li+ diffusion pathways. GITT measurements show deeper lithiation (x ≈ 0.65 vs 0.48 in LixMnO2) and a more homogeneous solid-solution-like intercalation regime in nanosized particles, avoiding bulk phase-transition kinetic bottlenecks. The nanosized cathode retains 70% capacity with ∼99.5% Coulombic efficiency after 400 cycles at 3C, demonstrating particle-size engineering as an effective strategy for high-rate, long-life advanced battery energy storage.
n4a785d0868cf: The development of aqueous zinc batteries is critically constrained by the electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability at the Zn anode. Herein, a zwitterionic dynamic buffering interface (ZDBI) is constructed by using trace glufosinate ammonium (GA). The dissociated GA– anchors onto the Zn(101) surface via its phosphinate and carboxylate groups with its protonated amino group (−NH3+) extending into the electrolyte to dynamically respond to interfacial electric fields. Meanwhile, free NH4+ cations can form an electrostatic shielding layer under an electric field. This synergistic chemisorbed-mobile-ion buffering network thickens the electric double layer, inhibits water-splitting parasitic reactions, and induces (101)-oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable cycling for over 7800 h with a cumulative capacity of 3.9 Ah cm–2, while Zn||Cu half-cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%, and Zn||V2O5 full cells retain 88% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g–1. This work offers an efficient strategy for addressing electrode–electrolyte interfacial issues.
n0fd77709f9e7: Emerging low-dimensional chiral perovskites have recently demonstrated significant application potential in circularly polarized light detection, spintronics, and quantum information technology due to their unique chiroptical activity and spin-selective properties. This review systematically summarizes their material systems, synthesis methods, chirality transfer mechanisms, and applications in photodetectors. The critical role of chiral organic cations in crystal regulation and chiroptical properties along with corresponding fabrication strategies is analyzed. Then, the inherent mechanisms of chirality transfer from organic to inorganic components are thoroughly discussed, encompassing structural distortion induction and electronic orbital coupling. Subsequently, recent advances in circularly polarized photodetectors based on low-dimensional chiral perovskites are highlighted from device performance, spin selection efficiency, to bio-inspired polarization vision systems. Finally, the challenges and future directions in this field are prospected. This review provides a comprehensive summarization for the development of low-dimensional chiral perovskites and their applications in next-generation polarized photodetectors.
nb960c4380d39: Hyperbolic media support high-k electromagnetic modes, enabling subdiffractional confinement, anomalous refraction, and enhanced light–matter interactions. While most hyperbolic metamaterials rely on artificial structuring, natural hyperbolicity arises from crystal anisotropy and direction-dependent plasma frequencies. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for natural hyperbolicity in copper chalcogenides by spectroscopic ellipsometry in the visible–near-infrared range. We demonstrate hyperbolic dispersion in bulk covellite CuS by identifying a spectral window where the real parts of the in-plane and out-of-plane permittivity components have opposite signs. The study is then expanded to size-controlled CuS nanosheets as oriented films. Using the Bruggeman effective medium approximation to account for the nanostructure/void composite, we show that hyperbolicity persists upon nanoscaling and that the epsilon-near-zero condition and hyperbolic bandwidth shift with size. Finally, we demonstrate analogous behavior in klockmannite CuSe nanosheets, establishing copper chalcogenides as a tunable platform for natural hyperbolicity at the boundary of the NIR and visible ranges.
n2fd16d2c42c9: Semiconductor hole spins offer a pathway to extended coherence times by decoupling from nuclear magnetic noise, while their spin–orbit coupling enables fast all-electrical control. In ZnSe, however, realizing this potential has been limited by p-doping challenges. Here, we circumvent this limit by optically activating acceptors and demonstrate optical spin initialization. We isolate a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor, confirmed by antibunching and accessed via the fast (244 ps) radiative recombination of a bound exciton. Magnetic and Raman spectroscopy reveal a spin-selective Λ system with an effective hole g-factor of 0.7 and an optical line width of 26.7 GHz. Time-resolved measurements reveal optical pumping of the hole spin with an estimated initialization fidelity of 90.7%. First-principles simulations combined with the experiment identify nitrogen as the most likely acceptor impurity. These results introduce a promising new platform for optically active spin qubits and single-photon sources in ZnSe.
n1a1405fdf060: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost and inherent safety. However, the practical use of an I2 cathode is severely restricted by poor electronic conductivity and the shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides. Herein, a synergistic scaffold composed of MXene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) modified with protonated polyaniline (PANI) via electrostatic interactions was designed. The MXene/CNT scaffold ensures overall conductivity and structural integrity. The protonated PANI immobilizes iodine species through nitrogen-containing groups and accelerates their interconversion, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. The MXene/CNTs/PANI-I2 cathode with an iodine loading of 43.96 wt % achieves a superior specific capacity of 150 mAh g–1 at a high rate of 20 C as well as excellent cycling stability over 10 000 cycles. This work offers a viable strategy for developing stable I2 cathodes for high-performance Zn–I2 batteries.
nf91d5f2e13a5: HfO2/ZrO2-based (HZO) materials are promising high-k dielectrics for integrated capacitors and advanced electronic devices. However, their performance is fundamentally constrained by polymorph competition and the trade-off between the dielectric constant and leakage current. Here, we report a stacking-engineered strategy that integrates HZO layers with optimized ferroelectric and dielectric properties separated by an Al2O3 interlayer (HAZO). A nonswitching pulse measurement is employed to exclude polarization-switching contributions and directly probe the intrinsic dielectric response. The optimized HAZO dielectric exhibits an enhanced dielectric constant while simultaneously suppressing leakage and improving the dielectric breakdown characteristics. Structural characterizations reveal that the engineered stacking stabilizes the coexistence of nonpolar tetragonal and polar orthorhombic phases and increases the phase-boundary density. This polymorphic configuration suppresses irreversible domain switching and enables a stable enhanced dielectric response. These results establish a robust pathway toward high-performance HZO-based dielectrics and provide key insights into tailoring dielectric properties through polymorphic-phase engineering.
n71f3585b7a45: Efforts to improve carbon dioxide electroreduction have often focused on the catalyst. Now, by focusing on the gas instead, non-thermal plasma activation can unlock products that are not accessible through conventional electrocatalysis.
nf495575612b6: Integrating distinct weaving topologies within a single molecular network creates coupled deformation modes and adaptive adsorption behaviour, pointing to a shift from constructing molecular topologies to exploiting them for functions.
n860fed4f84de: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.
n8cf20cf25776: Upon irradiation with visible light (λ = 425 nm), a tetrapeptide with a C-terminal photocatalytic site and an N-terminal site for substrate recognition promotes photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. The required spatial proximity of catalyst and substrate is corroborated by NMR spectroscopy studies and molecular dynamics simulations.
neab46ce06322: Access to silylium ions with three different substituents has remained elusive owing to substituent scrambling under established synthetic methods. Now, harnessing the Lewis superacidity of halogen-substituted silylium ions, a broadly applicable protocol for synthesizing such heteroleptic silylium ions without substituent redistribution by halide abstraction from readily available halosilanes is reported.
n735725c0eb15: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) utilizing either a ferroelectric dielectric (FeD) or a ferroelectric semiconductor (FeS) are highly promising for neuromorphic computing. While integrating FeD with emerging FeS could provide new degrees of freedom for synaptic plasticity, direct integration inevitably suffers from unintended electrostatic coupling and a lack of independent polarization control. Here, we demonstrate a structurally decoupled dual-ferroelectric field-effect transistor (Dual-FeFET) based on an α-In2Se3/ZrO2/HZO heterostructure, in which a ferroelectric dielectric and a ferroelectric semiconductor are integrated into a single transistor while retaining independent functional roles. The inserted ZrO2 interfacial layer mitigates unintended polarization coupling between HZO and α-In2Se3, enabling two orthogonal memory operations: gate-bias-induced HZO polarization switching globally modulates the carrier density of the α-In2Se3 channel, whereas drain-bias-induced α-In2Se3 polarization switching predominantly modulates the drain-side Schottky barrier near the contact region. Dual-mode PFM, Hall-bar analysis, temperature-dependent transport measurements, and ZrO2-thickness-dependent control experiments support the largely decoupled modulation of channel transport and contact injection. By sequentially exploiting these two modulation modes, the Dual-FeFET extends the conductance dynamic range and improves the linearity of synaptic potentiation compared with conventional single-mode FeFET operation. The device exhibits robust nonvolatile memory characteristics with stable endurance over 105 cycles and retention up to 105 s. When implemented in convolutional neural network simulations for CIFAR-10 image recognition, the Dual-FeFET-based synapses achieve an accuracy of 89.2%, approaching the ideal software accuracy of 96.5% and outperforming conventional single-FeFET-based synapses (74.1%). These results demonstrate that structural ferroelectric decoupling enables independently programmable channel and contact modulation in multifunctional 2D ferroelectric transistors.
n828307d5b742: Effective transdermal drug delivery (TDD) demands both the ability to bypass the stratum corneum (ST) and the robustness to sustain delivery efficiency under real-life conditions. Despite advances in nanocarriers, microneedles, and electrostimulation, many TDDS strategies face limitations due to cytotoxicity, invasiveness, device dependence, and poor performance for large molecules in real-world conditions. In this study, we present a marine-inspired TDDS patch (PDA@SC) that integrates adhesion strategies from marine organisms to achieve stable skin attachment and atraumatic macromolecular delivery, even on dynamic skin surfaces. The suction-cup (SC) structure, inspired by octopus’ suckers, generates negative pressure upon preload-induced deformation, promoting temporary mechanical modulation for nanolevel control of the ST barrier and enhancing drug delivery without external power. Simultaneously, the mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating modifies hydrophobic surfaces into high surface energy interfaces capable of chemical bonding, thereby ensuring intimate adhesion and minimizing drug leakage. Experimental findings confirmed that the delivery of the high molecular weight compound was enhanced on deformed skin, showing a 600% improvement compared to conventional topical application. In addition, preliminary human evaluation demonstrated that PDA@SC effectively improved key dermatological parameters. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of PDA@SC as a platform that can drive technological progress in wearable therapeutics and cosmetics.
n02dac954595f: Ovarian cancer, the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, urgently demands early and accurate diagnostic methods. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tEVs) hold great promise as noninvasive biomarkers, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by inherent heterogeneity and the inability of conventional assays to detect multiple types of biomarkers. To break this bottleneck, we developed a novel one-pot, triple-encoding platform that integrates size–fluorescence-encoded beads with a membrane fusion strategy. This enables simultaneous in situ profiling of 11 miRNAs across three distinct EV subpopulations defined by EpCAM/PD-L1 expression. Leveraging machine learning, an 11-miRNA logistic panel achieved tumor versus health discrimination (AUC = 0.995), and a combinatorial signature based on EV subpopulations and miRNA profiles enabled the classification of ovarian cancer subtypes, achieving 78.6% accuracy in the validation cohort. Our work provides a versatile and scalable approach for multiparameter EV analysis, enabling comprehensive EV miRNA profiling and ovarian cancer classification.
n9132843f657f: This work presents a flexible, self‐healing supercapacitor (SHSC) comprising an MXene/graphene nanoscrolls@carbon cloth (MXene/GNS@CC) composite electrode and a self‐healing poly(vinyl alcohol)‐polydopamine (PVA‐PDA) hydrogel electrolyte. The MXene/GNS@CC electrode was directly fabricated on carbon cloth through a one‐step electrophoretic deposition (EPD) strategy, in which graphene nanoscrolls (GNS) were interwoven among the MXene nanosheets to construct a three‐dimensional (3D) interpenetrating architecture. This architecture suppressed nanosheet restacking, increased accessible surface area, facilitated ion transport, and improved mechanical reliability. The resulting electrode was further integrated with a self‐healingPVA‐PDA hydrogel electrolyte to assemble an all‐in‐one supercapacitor. Owing to the abundant catechol groups in PDA, the hydrogel electrolyte exhibited excellent self‐healing capability and strong interfacial adhesion. Moreover, hydrogen‐bonding interactions with the terminal groups on the MXene surface and π–π conjugation interactions with GNS contributed to the formation of a robust 3D network. Consequently, the MXene/GNS@CC electrode delivered an areal capacitance of 6880.60 mF·cm−2 at 1 mA·cm−2. The assembled SHSC achieved an areal capacitance of 1152.03 mF·cm−2 at 1 mA·cm−2 and an areal energy density of 195.37 µWh·cm−2 at a power density of 0.61 mW·cm−2. Additionally, the device retained 87.32% of its initial capacitance even after four cutting/healing cycles, indicating its broad application prospects in the field of flexible self‐healing energy‐storage devices.
nbd7e5a889f48: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted widespread attention from researchers worldwide and experienced rapid development in recent years. The bottom interface plays a crucial role in charge transfer and collection, and its status significantly affect the perovskite crystallization and the performance of PSCs. Thus, in this work, potassium trifluoromethanesulfonate (KFMA), was introduced as a multifunctional molecular bridge at the SnO2/Perovskite bottom interface to improve the interface status and the efficiency and stability of PSCs. Our results show that KFMA can interact with SnO2, passivate its surface defects, and optimize the interface energy level alignment, leading to enhanced charge transfer and promoted carrier extraction. Additionally, KFMA can regulate the growth of PbI2 and perovskite crystallization, making more thorough transformation from PbI2 to perovskite, giving a high‐quality perovskite film. As a result, PSCs with a KFMA interface layer achieved an efficiency of 26.08% and long‐term stability. After maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1 Sun illumination for 500 h, PCE of the KFMA‐based device remained at 82.6% of the initial efficiency, while that of the pristine PSC just was left about 40%.
nc4b988c7dcbc: The deployment of 5G/6G communication systems demands microwave dielectric ceramics that simultaneously possess a near‐zero temperature coefficient of resonant frequency and an ultra‐low dielectric loss (tanδ), which represents a long‑standing challenge that demands effective optimization strategies. Herein, the fundamental limitation is substantially alleviated by a strategy integrating interpretable machine learning with entropy engineering, enabling the reverse design of a medium‐entropy perovskite microwave ceramic composition (Ca0.7Sm0.27Nd0.03)[Ti0.686(Mg1/3Nb2/3)0.014Al0.3]O3. This ceramic material delivers a desired combination perfomance of τf = −0.18 ppm/°C and tanδ = 1.19 × 10−4 at 4.6 GHz. Multiscale characterization reveals that entropy‐induced chemical disorder creates isolated polar nanoregions that pin charged defects, transforming them from a source of relaxation loss into static structural units, which is different from the conventional defect–loss correlation mechanism. The optimized ceramic is implemented in a dielectric resonator antenna, which demonstrates superior performance: a radiation efficiency of 96.2% and a gain of 6.06 dBi. The findings establish a generalizable framework for navigating complex compositional spaces and resolving conflicting properties in perovskite materials.
nb3ab9a082686: The evolution from monomeric to dimeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) opens new opportunities for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet stronger π–π interactions in these larger architectures risk inducing aggregation over ordered assembly, making it challenging to maintain a well‐balanced intermolecular packing. We design a symmetric indenocarbazole dimer (DIC) to harness cooperative face‐to‐face and edge‐to‐edge π–π stacking for directing intermolecular attraction into ordered, long‐range assembly rather than uncontrolled aggregation. In stark contrast, its asymmetric indenocarbazole‐carbazole conjugate (ICCB) suffers from random clustering and incomplete passivation. This ordered SAM template provides a homogeneous foundation for perovskite crystallization, delivering a champion PCE of 26.33% with an outstanding FF of 86.62%, significantly outperforming ICCB (24.80%), while retaining over 85% of its initial efficiency after 1600 h. Our findings establish molecular symmetry and dual‐directional π–π interactions as critical design principles for high‐performance dimeric SAMs.
nc495f1d8f4ad: Selective CO2‐to‐formate electroreduction requires oxygen‐deficient SnOx sites that stabilize O‐bound *OCHO intermediates while resisting cathodic over‐reduction. Here, we use a precursor‐level coordination competition strategy to construct an oxygen vacancy (Ov)‐rich SnOx catalyst coupled with isolated Cu–N sites through controlled conversion of amino‐functionalized Cu/Sn metal‐organic frameworks. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2‐aminoterephthalic acid (H2BDC‐NH2) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnOx domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand‐derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu‐SnOx/NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy‐related SnOx environments and predominantly isolated Cu–N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O‐bound *OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnOx. Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate‐related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu‐SnOx/NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm−2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. Half‐cell and full‐cell energy efficiencies (EE) of 65% and 54%, respectively, were achieved in the flow cell and membrane electrode assembly (MEA). This work provides a coordination‐competition strategy for durable high‐rate CO2 electroreduction.
n38f2bf41a754: Functional separators that regulate ion transport before lithium ions (Li+) reach the lithium metal surface are critical for mitigating dendritic deposition and interfacial instability in lithium metal batteries. However, most separator designs mainly emphasize Li+ affinity or electrolyte wettability, while the migration and decomposition behavior of anions remains insufficiently controlled. Herein, a coordination-gated anion-sieving separator is developed by constructing a UiO-66@F-COF@Ni core–shell interlayer on commercial polypropylene. In this architecture, the UiO-66 core provides stable porous transport channels, and the fluorinated imine-linked COF shell creates a polar ion-regulating interface. The introduced Ni2+ coordination centers interact with PF6 − to modulate anion migration and interfacial decomposition. Benefiting from the coupled MOF@COF heterointerface and anion-sieving effect, the separator exhibits high ionic conductivity, enhanced Li+ transference, and reduced interfacial resistance. The regulated ion flux alleviates concentration polarization, guides uniform Li deposition, and promotes the formation of a compact inorganic-rich SEI. Consequently, LFP||Li batteries retain 126.1 mAh g−1 after 1200 cycles at 2.0 C, and high-voltage NCM811||Li batteries maintain 141.4 mAh g−1 after 600 cycles at 3.0 C. This coordination-regulated MOF@COF separator provides a practical strategy for stable, high-rate, and high-voltage lithium metal batteries.
n4035cae876e9: Plasmon‐mediated catalysis provides a promising route for enhancing photocatalytic hydrogen generation from ammonia borane (NH3BH3), yet the reaction rate remains limited by insufficient charge generation and separation. Herein, we address this limitation by developing a plasmonic coupling strategy to generate enhanced local electromagnetic fields in a ternary Co0.5Cu0.5/Mo.
