Cu nanoparticles are dispersed on Mo and Co nanosheets are anchored on Mo and extend toward the Cu nanoparticles. Co0.5Cu0.5/Mo catalyst achieves an outstanding turnover frequency of 162.8 min−1 under steady‐state H2 flow for photocatalytic NH3BH3 hydrolysis at 298 K, outperforming Co/Mo and Cu/Mo by factors of approximately 1.5 and 5.0, respectively, and surpassing most reported noble‐metal‐free catalysts under comparable conditions. Combined spectroscopic characterizations, surface enhanced Raman scattering, in situ x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations reveal that the synergistic plasmonic coupling between Mo with a partially oxidized surface and Cu intensifies the local electromagnetic field, promotes charge generation and separation, and induces preferential electron accumulation on Cu. This redistribution enlarges the electron density difference between Cu and Co active sites, thereby facilitating the activation of NH3BH3 and H2O and accelerating hydrogen evolution. This study provides a feasible strategy for engineering electromagnetic‐field‐enhanced non‐precious‐metal catalysts for NH3BH3 hydrolysis and related hydrogen‐generation reactions.
nd76eede7dc34: Selective oxidation of urea to nitrite (NO2 −) rather than N2 is desireable for Direct urea fuel cells (DUFCs), doubling the electron yield per molecule while suppressing gas accumulation. Herein, we report a NiCoOOH model catalyst in which cobalt incorporation stabilizes electron-delocalized states around Ni sites, thereby steering the oxidation pathway toward selective urea-to-nitrite conversion. In situ Raman and infrared spectroscopies reveal that NiCoOOH triggers the formation of hydroxyl oxide species at potentials as low as 1.32 V vs. RHE while simultaneously promoting urea adsorption. The markedly attenuated *CO2 vibrational signal indicates suppression of the N2-evolution and supports a reaction pathway in which OH− preferentially attacks the C─N bond. Consequently, NiCoOOH achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 84.7% for liquid nitrogen oxides (NOx −), representing a 21.5% improvement over Ni(OH)2, and requires only 1.48 V to deliver 500 mA cm−2 with stable operation for 100 h. Leveraging these advantages, the catalyst enables a 380 mV voltage saving in urea-assisted water splitting. Furthermore, a flow-type DUFC affords a peak power density of 18.98 mW cm−2, and a pouch-type DUFC successfully powers an LED and an electronic timer, confirming the practical viability of this urea-to-nitrite strategy in energy devices.
n1fbfd85ade41: Interface engineering is vital for improving the efficiency of semiconductor‐based solar energy devices. Herein, we report a dipole‐induced dynamic interface engineering strategy enabled by the nematic phase of 2‐(4‐((4‐(heptyloxy)phenyl)ethynyl)phenyl)‐5‐methylbenzo[d]oxazole (PEMB‐N) liquid crystal molecules. The rationally designed BiVO4/PEMB‐N/FeNiOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.4 mA/cm2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, alongside a solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency of 7.2% and sustained photostability. A combination of density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental characterizations (in situ UV/vis spectroelectrochemistry and Kelvin probe force microscopy) elucidates that the enhanced dipole moment arising from benzoxazole functionalization, coupled with the dynamically tunable nematic phase of PEMB‐N, facilitates the directional and multichannel extraction and migration of holes across the BiVO4/PEMB‐N interface. Furthermore, at the PEMB‐N/FeNiOOH interface, the well‐ordered nematic phase effectively modulates the Fe d‐band center and boosts the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. Importantly, this strategy is universally applicable to Ti‐Fe2O3/PEMB‐N/FeNiOOH photoanodes, demonstrating its broad compatibility with different photoanodes. These findings provide a “soft” interface engineering concept compared to conventional “rigid” interface modulation strategies for constructing high‐performance solar‐driven water splitting systems.
n11a4621d9e45: Photothermal therapy (PTT), photodynamic therapy (PDT), and NIR‑II fluorescence imaging are each compromised by tumor hypoxia, thermotolerance, and insufficient contrast, respectively, limiting the efficacy of integrated phototheranostics. To address these challenges, we developed a multi‑amplification theranostic nanoplatform (ReCO‐TPP NPs) that initially exhibits weak NIR‐II fluorescence, type I PDT, and PTT, yet undergoes substantial self‐amplification upon light irradiation. A rhenium(I) carbonyl complex was covalently conjugated to a D‐π‐A‐π‐D fluorophore (DTP), and the heavy‐metal center partially quenches the NIR‐II emission and suppresses type I ROS generation. Upon tumor accumulation and 808 nm laser irradiation, the limited initial ROS cleave the rhenium‐carbonyl bond, releasing CO and regenerating the free DTP fluorophore. This activation dramatically amplifies NIR‐II brightness and type I photodynamic activity, while maintaining excellent photothermal performance. The liberated CO suppresses heat shock protein 70, dissipates mitochondrial membrane potential, and inhibits ATP synthesis, thereby sensitizing tumor cells to PTT and establishing a self‐reinforcing ROS‐CO‐ROS cycle. Mitochondrial targeting via triphenylphosphonium further intensifies cellular damage. In 4T1 tumor‐bearing mice, ReCO‐TPP NPs enable deep‐tissue NIR‐II imaging with post‐irradiation brightness enhancement and produce potent synergistic antitumor efficacy. This molecularly engineered “weak‐to‐strong” theranostic strategy offers a promising paradigm for precisely amplified cancer phototheranostics.
n02e37d9085cb: Introducing multidentate organic passivators has emerged as an effective strategy for defect passivation at the buried interface of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the active polar functional groups within these passivators are prone to supramolecular polymerization, which compromises passivation effectiveness. Herein, a supramolecular depolymerization strategy synergistically driven by thermal annealing and heteromolecular interactions is proposed. This approach enables the in situ depolymerization of the Zaltoprofen (Za) supramolecular structures introduced at the buried interface. The resulting depolymerized Za molecules are effectively anchored onto the underlying hole transport layer (HTL), while their molecular orientation is optimized to expose Lewis base coordination sites toward the perovskite layer. Consequently, enhanced coordination interactions with undercoordinated Pb2+ are achieved, leading to more effective interfacial defect passivation and improved charge extraction. As a result, inverted PSCs based on a 1.57 eV bandgap perovskite exhibit a significantly improved power conversion efficiency (PCE), increasing from 24.05% to 25.61%. Moreover, the devices treated with this strategy demonstrate substantially enhanced operational stability compared with the pristine devices. This work provides a simple and effective strategy for activating supramolecular passivators and maximizing their defect‐passivation capability in high‐efficiency inverted PSCs.
n8a31158fa21f: Selective electrochemical upgrading of ethylene glycol (EG) to glycolic acid (GA) coupled with hydrogen evolution provides a promising pathway for chemical‐energy co‐production, yet remains challenged by CO poisoning, excessive C‐C bond cleavage, and uncontrolled oxygenated intermediates on Pt‐based catalysts. This work develops a platinum‐based high‐entropy intermetallic catalyst (Pt4FeCoNiCu) anchored on phosphorus‐nitrogen co‐doped porous carbon (HEI‐PNC) for selective EG oxidation and hydrogen evolution. The ordered intermetallic lattice creates chemically diverse atomic environments that regulate interfacial water structures and oxygenated intermediate evolution during EG oxidation, thereby suppressing CO poisoning and unwanted C─C bond cleavage. Meanwhile, electronic redistribution within the intermetallic lattice stabilizes key C2 intermediates and accelerates reaction kinetics. Consequently, HEI‐PNC delivers a low onset potential of 0.304 V, a 4.4‐fold enhancement in Pt mass activity compared with Pt/C and achieves a glycolate Faradaic efficiency of 98.2%. Integrated into a hybrid alkali/acid fuel cell, the catalyst enables self‐powered co‐production of glycolate and H2 with stable operation over 220 h. This work highlights interfacial water‐regulated high‐entropy intermetallic catalysis as an effective strategy for selective polyol upgrading and chemical‐energy co‐production.
n2ecf0f22566f: With the development of visible, hyperspectral, and thermal‐infrared multi‐band reconnaissance technologies, achieving an ideal camouflage in the jungle environment remains a major challenge. Inspired by green leaves, this work designs and prepares a flame‐retardant and robust biomimetic porous hydrogel (BPH), which not only mimics the color and visible‐near‐infrared reflectance spectral characteristics of natural leaves, but also simulates the moisture absorption‐transpiration behavior for thermal management. The color difference between BPH and leaf is only 1.87, making them barely distinguishable by naked eyes. Importantly, BPH exhibits a visible‐near infrared reflectance spectrum similar to that of natural leaf, with the spectral correlation coefficient and cosine similarity as high as 0.940 and 0.958, respectively. In addition, the radiative temperature difference between BPH and surrounding leaves does not exceed 2°C. Furthermore, BPH could serve as a coating to endow conventional fabrics with superior visible, hyperspectral, and thermal infrared camouflage performance in outdoor jungle environments, thereby acting as camouflage barriers such as tents and camouflage nets. This work provides a novel strategy for the design and preparation of visible, hyperspectral, and thermal infrared camouflage materials, aiming to address the challenge of multi‐band camouflage compatibility and enhance the battlefield survivability of targets.
n779b869f4e07: CO2‐assisted ethane dehydrogenation (CO2‐EDH) combines olefin production with CO2 conversion, yet suffers from high temperatures and catalyst instability in thermal catalysis. This work establishes an alternating current magnetic field (ACMF)‐mediated catalytic system using Fe3O4 decorated on iron foam (Fe3O4/IF) as the induction catalyst, achieving significant enhancement of the CO2‐EDH process under mild conditions. At 500°C, a temperature 200°C lower than that required in conventional thermal catalysis to reach a comparable conversion level, the system realized an ethane conversion of 22.2% with 97% ethylene selectivity. At an equivalent conversion level, the catalyst stability was improved by 15‐fold compared to traditional thermal catalysis, with continuous stable operation for 80 h. The eddy current effect induced by the alternating magnetic field promotes electron transfer between Fe and Fe3O4 and accelerates the oxygen redox cycle, thereby enhancing the reaction kinetics of the CO2‐EDH process based on the Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) mechanism. This work provides an effective approach for improving the performance of alkane dehydrogenation under mild conditions and contributes new insights to the field of magnetically induced catalysis.
na1ccb5e5df41: Van der Waals (vdW) heterointerfaces provide a versatile platform for tailoring polarization‐resolved excitonic emission in 2D semiconductors, offering new opportunities for polarization‐encoded photonic functionalities. However, the realization of distinct and externally reconfigurable polarization orientations for coexisting excitonic states within a single magnetic heterostructure remains largely unexplored. Here we demonstrate magnetically reconfigurable exciton polarization in a MoSe2/CrOCl/Fe3GaTe2 vdW heterostructure, arising from the combined effects of interfacial symmetry breaking and magnetically mediated interfacial coupling. Polarization‐resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal pronounced in‐plane anisotropy for both neutral excitons (X0) and trions (T), with strongly non‐collinear polarization axes. Near the spin‐flop transition of CrOCl, the emission polarization undergoes an abrupt ∼ 90°rotation under an applied magnetic field, generating bistable polarization states that allow optical readout of magnetic phase evolution and dual‐channel polarization encoding. A further reorientation across the Néel temperature highlights the intimate coupling between magnetic order and lattice symmetry at the heterointerface. First‐principles calculations attribute the emergent anisotropy to anisotropic charge redistribution in MoSe2. These findings establish magnetic vdW heterointerfaces as a route to reconfigurable multi‐exciton polarization control and magnetic‐field‐tunable polarization encoding in 2D materials.
nd67a28c72229: Strong interactions between large dipole moment additives and host materials have been widely used to modulate molecular packing in organic solar cells (OSCs), while most studies focuses on dipole moment magnitude instead of the polarization properties orientation. Here, we challenge this oversimplified view by demonstrating that the polarization properties orientation—determined by both dipole orientation and polarizability anisotropy, rather than dipole magnitude alone – is the important factor. To quantify this, we introduce the “polarization properties orientation coupling degree” (P), which quantifies the matching of dipole orientation and polarizability distribution between additives and acceptors. Employing 1,4‐diiodobenzene (DIB) and 1,3,5‐triiodobenzene (TIB) as additives in the PM6:Y6 system with identical dipole moment magnitude but different orientation, we find that TIB exhibits a much higher p value (1.455 vs. 0.191), resulting in stronger intermolecular interactions. Consequently, TIB induces the formation of S‐type and S′‐type dimers of Y6, which optimizes exciton and charge transport behavior, boosting the performance from 17.53% to 18.08%. Furthermore, this principle is validated in high‐performance systems of PM6:L8‐BO (19.33%) and PM6:BTP‐eC9 (19.23%), and shows significant advantages in large‐area fabrication and reproducibility. This study highlights the significant role of polarization properties orientation, offering rational design strategy for high‐performance OSCs.
n8c7be01e4664: The advancement of birefringent materials is critical for next-generation integrated photonics, yet conventional systems face intrinsic limitations in birefringence magnitude. Sulfate crystals offer a promising platform but have been hindered by their dependence on specific metal cations and insufficient optical anisotropy. Here, we report a molecular design strategy that overcomes these constraints by employing linearly extended π-conjugated organic cations as high-anisotropy building units. Through rational amino-functionalization of C12H8N2, we engineer the novel cation [H2(C12H10N4)]2 +, which exhibits an exceptional polarizability anisotropy of 156.7 a.u. Using a mild aqueous route, a metal-free sulfate crystal, [H2(C12H10N4)]SO4·3H2O was synthesized, which achieves a record birefringence of 0.981 at 550 nm, surpassing all known sulfate birefringent materials and outperforming commercial benchmarks and setting a new performance standard for birefringent sulfates. Structural analysis reveals that the cations align via hydrogen-bond-directed assembly with sulfate tetrahedra into a quasi-two-dimensional anisotropic structure, thereby maximizing the macroscopic optical response. This study demonstrates that incorporating linearly extended π-conjugated organic building blocks into sulfate frameworks sever as a robust strategy for discovering highly birefringent crystals.
n044e61295b52: Postoperative recurrence and metastasis in breast cancer remain major clinical challenges, primarily driven by persistent inflammation responses and secondary infections at surgical sites. These pathological processes trigger sphingolipid dysregulation and generate the redox imbalance for sustaining a chronic inflammation‐metabolism feedback loop and promoting tumor regeneration. However, current therapeutic modalities frequently exhibit insufficient capacity to concomitantly attenuate inflammatory cascades, scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS), and restore metabolic homeostasis. Herein, we developed a multifunctional injectable botanicals/nanozyme hydrogel (CGHD) that restores redox balance and reprograms sphingolipid metabolism to inhibit tumor relapse. Under near‐infrared irradiation, CGHD triggered cascade catalytic reactions that scavenged ROS and downregulated sphingosine and sphingosine kinase‐1, thereby disrupting the inflammation–metabolism feedback loop driving tumor regeneration. In postoperative breast cancer models, CGHD accelerated wound healing and significantly suppressed recurrence and metastasis of residual tumors. Multi‐omics analyses further showed that CGHD alleviated oxidative stress, remodeled sphingolipid metabolism, and suppressed NF‐κB and TNF signaling. These effects decreased IL‐6 and TNF‐α expression while increasing IL‐10 levels. Collectively, these findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a therapeutic target linking oxidative stress, inflammation, and postoperative tumor progression, highlighting CGHD as a promising strategy for recurrence prevention.
nf7608d5016a0: Shortwave infrared (SWIR) photodetection and imaging are of increasing importance for many emerging applications, such as optical and quantum communications, night vision, biomedical imaging and sensing. While planar InGaAs and Ge-based SWIR photodetectors are the current state-of-the-art, it is challenging to achieve single-photon level sensitivity at non-cryogenic temperatures due to their high dark current and thermal noise. Here, we demonstrate a highly sensitive self-powered InGaAs nanowire photodetector with single-photon-level sensitivity at 1310 nm. The device utilizes a p+ InGaAs/Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) radial heterojunction nanowire structure, enabling strong optical confinement and efficient carrier extraction. It demonstrates a detection sensitivity down to 118.1 pW at room temperature and 6.5 pW at 223 K, corresponding to two photons per pulse of a 1310 nm laser excitation at 20 MHz with the noise equivalent powers of 1.59 × 10−13 W Hz−1/2 and 2.18 × 10−15 W Hz−1/2 respectively. The photodetector maintains a high signal-to-noise ratio of 58 dB at 1550 nm and cut-off frequency of 15 MHz. Also, single-pixel imaging under illumination down to ∼580 µW cm− 2, showcasing the robust imaging capability under extremely low-light conditions. Our results highlight the potential of nanowire-based heterojunction photodetectors for the development of next-generation, low-cost, high-performance SWIR photodetection and imaging technology.
naee179605212: α‐In2Se3 ferroelectric semiconductor field‐effect transistors (FeS‐FETs) offer attractive non‐volatile memory characteristics but are limited by high source/drain (S/D) contact resistance and inefficient ferroelectric polarization switching. Here, we demonstrate a low‐temperature, CMOS‐compatible strain‐engineering strategy based on region‐dependent in‐plane (IP) lattice strain. A silicon nitride stress layer induces tensile strain in the S/D regions and compressive strain in the channel, producing spatially differentiated effects within a single device. The contact‐side tensile strain modifies the interfacial electronic structure and reduces contact resistance, whereas the channel‐side compressive strain facilitates ferroelectric polarization switching. Consequently, the strained α‐In2Se3 FeS‐FET achieves a 12.03‐fold reduction in S/D contact resistance, a 19.21‐fold increase in on‐state current, a 4.4%p increase in normalized memory window, and a 22.4‐fold enhancement in the ferroelectric resistance switching ratio. Raman characterization and finite‐element method simulations establish the region‐dependent strain distribution, while interface‐pinning analysis and first‐principles calculations provide mechanistic support for the distinct contact‐ and channel‐side effects. These results establish region‐dependent IP lattice strain as a unified device‐engineering framework for jointly controlling contact transport and ferroelectric memory functionality in vdW α‐In2Se3 FeS‐FETs.
n4b7b4e1fb974: The convergence of neural interfaces, wearable bioelectronics, and human‐machine interaction is driving intelligent biointerfaces capable of sensing and responding to neural, physiological, and biomechanical signals. Realizing this vision demands a substantial advance in sensing and actuation hardware, which remains constrained by trade‐offs in conventional bulk materials. This review proposes that two‐dimensional framework materials, encompassing intrinsic 2D crystals, heterostructures, composites, and low‐dimensional architectures, provide a transformative platform to overcome these barriers. The application scope is organized into five categories: implantable neural interfaces, non‐invasive neural interfaces, physiological sensing, wearable human‐machine interfaces, and soft actuation or haptic feedback. We establish a three‐tier architecture. First, we catalog the requirements of piezoresistive, piezoelectric, capacitive, electromagnetic, electrostatic, and electrothermal sensors and actuators, identifying performance bottlenecks in bulk materials. Second, we trace these ceilings to microscopic origins: continuous electronic density of states, strong dielectric screening, coupled elastic‐thermal phonon transport, and weakly tunable electron‐phonon coupling that lock sensitivity, compliance, energy efficiency, and thermal safety into trade‐offs. Third, we show how quantum confinement, attenuated screening, and broken symmetry in 2D materials decouple these constraints. We conclude by outlining a co‐design strategy integrating heavy‐element doping, symmetry engineering, interfacial design, and coupling phenomena to tailor 2D materials for next‐generation intelligent biointerfaces.
nfbe73a3b3b48: Dynamic helicity control in the terahertz (THz) regime is essential for ultrafast polarization optics, chiral spectroscopy, and polarization‐selective photonic devices, yet remains difficult because most THz chiral systems are structurally fixed or rely on slow external tuning. To address this, we report a curved Ni split‐ring metasurface enabling magnetically amplified and ultrafast reconfigurable THz helicity control. Handed curvature breaks mirror symmetry and produces opposite static circular dichroism in left‐handed and right‐handed metasurfaces, accompanied by a near order‐of‐magnitude increase in current asymmetry compared to flat and achiral references. In pump‐free steady‐state THz transmission, in‐plane magnetization increases the static CD contrast from 9.4 to 33.6 (3.57‐fold enhancement). In optical pump–THz probe measurements, magnetization further increases the normalized transient circular dichroism contrast from 0.538 to 1.553 (2.89‐fold enhancement). The magnetized response exhibits switching‐like TRCD reweighting within τ ≈ 0.5 ps, consistent with ultrafast transient helicity control. These results show that femtosecond excitation reweights a pre‐existing magneto‐geometric chiral state rather than creating an independent photoinduced chiral structure. This work provides a lithography‐compatible route to ultrafast, reversible, and magnetically enhanced THz helicity control.
nd145a09616ed: Type-I photosensitization addresses the dilemma of intracellular bacterial hypoxia-induced photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) inefficacy, yet precise targeting and eradicating sequestered pathogens remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we engineer an albumin-based photodynamic conversion nanoparticles integrating target-specific recognition with controlled antibacterial functions to precisely eliminate intracellular pathogens and restore infected cell activity. Mechanistic studies reveal a vertically-crossed conformation that promotes intramolecular electron transfer and charge separation, redirecting photosensitizer (PS) reactivity toward type-I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Electron-rich albumin further enhances cationic PS+• recycling, photostability, and O2 −• production, while its selective cytoplasmic delivery via receptor/charge interactions enables preferential accumulation in intracellular bacteria, with reduced off-target organelle engagement. We demonstrate application in S. aureus-infected sepsis showing high type-I ROS levels for antibacterial function from the nanoparticles to restore redox and immune homeostasis without noticeable toxicity. This work pioneers a conformationally-gated ROS conversion approach for eliminating intracellular bacterial infections, merging mechanistic precision with therapeutic potential for clinical sepsis management.
n02a41675d0c2: Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion-symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac-frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight-binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier-free value for Δ below the nearest-neighbour hopping amplitude t, and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t. Momentum-space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein-tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω-shaped and power-splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s− 1. Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high-capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.
n151b1d46b21c: Controlling crystallization kinetics of FAPbI3 perovskite is crucial for improving crystal quality, device performance and stability. Herein, we report a sustained-release strategy to regulate the PbI2-to-FAPbI3 conversion. PbI2 lattice expansion arising from the interaction between PEI (oligomeric poly(ethyleneimine)) and iodide species suppresses nonuniform PbI2 crystallization and facilitates FAI infiltration. Moreover, the weak interaction between oligomeric PEGDE (poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether) and FAI slows the reaction between FAI and PbI2, leading to homogeneous phase conversion during annealing. Consequently, enlarged FAPbI3 grains are obtained with improved crystallographic orientation, reduced strain and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Furthermore, released PEI and PEGDE undergo in situ crosslinking to form a three-dimensional network that passivates grain boundaries, stabilizes microstructure and affords inner encapsulation. The resulting champion n-i-p device presents a power conversion efficiency of 26.6% (certified 26.17%). Both films and devices exhibit enhanced photothermal stability. The PEI/PEGDE-treated device maintains 92% of its initial efficiency at 85 °C for over 1,100 h, 96% after continuous illumination (∼100 mW cm− 2) and maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking for over 1,500 h, and 89% after MPP tracking at 85 °C over 12 days. This work offers a polymerization-assisted route for synchronizing crystallization control, defect passivation and inner encapsulation to enhance perovskite solar-cell stability.
n14a430ad08e1: Two‐dimensional (2D) materials have gained tremendous attention for their structural diversity and versatile functionality. However, conventional synthesis and post‐synthetic modification often provide limited control over where and how structural or chemical changes occur, restricting the precise tailoring of composition, atomic configuration, and electronic structure. Topochemical engineering offers a distinct approach by directing chemical reactions at predefined sites while preserving key structural features of parent materials, thereby enabling precise and selective modulation at the atomic and molecular levels through four core strategies: conversion, termination, substitution, and transformation. Herein, we present a systematic and critical review of the latest advances in the topochemical engineering of MXenes and other representative 2D materials (TE‐2DMs). We establish the conceptual framework and classification criteria for these strategies and discuss their implementation and underlying structural regulation mechanisms. Special emphasis is placed on the structure–performance correlations of TE‐2DMs in electrochemical energy storage and conversion. We further summarize general design principles and practical guidelines for selecting and implementing appropriate topochemical strategies. Finally, we identify key challenges and emerging opportunities in this rapidly evolving field, with the aim of guiding the rational design of high‐performance 2D functional materials for next‐generation electrochemical energy technologies.
n878cdac60aef: Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.
n6ce9576b7864: While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.
n3ac09470549c: Stacked scintillators for x‐ray energy discrimination require at least two emission bands with sufficient spectral separation to avoid signal crosstalk. Rare‐earth‐based double perovskites exhibit narrow‐band luminescence at multiple visible wavelengths, which is advantageous for such designs. However, an efficient narrow‐band blue emission has not yet been realized, hindering further development. Here, efficient Eu2+ blue luminescence is achieved in Cs2(Li/Na/K)(Lu/Y/Gd)Cl6 under ambient conditions via photo‐induced reduction of Eu3+ to Eu2+, eliminating harsh reducing atmospheres. The reduction is driven by 254 nm UV or x‐ray irradiation, while mild heating and x‐ray‐induced lattice distortion assist carrier migration. The unique multi‐cation structure provides cation vacancies that trap holes, stabilizing the reduction. The resulting Eu2+ emits narrow‐band blue light at 450 nm (FWHM 25 nm, PLQY 84.1%, 19 000 ph/MeV) in Cs2NaLuCl6, and coexisting Eu3+ shows narrow‐band red emission, achieving a 144 nm spectral separation. Taking advantage of this well‐separated dual emission, a stacked scintillator device enables highly material‐discriminative x‐ray imaging.
n3a0704437377: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck in anodic water splitting because of sluggish adsorption and desorption kinetics of O-containing intermediates. Optimizing the adsorption strength of various O-containing intermediates in accordance with the Sabatier principle involves the precise tuning of the active-site electronic structure. Herein, we explore a p-block metal-assisted synergism regulation strategy in NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) by introducing group-13 elements (Al, Ga, In) as dopants. Among various doped LDHs, In-doped NiFe-LDH shows the highest OER activity by demanding an overpotential value of 298 mV at 10 mA/cm2 along with enhanced intrinsic turnover frequency and long-term stability. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals that In3+ preferentially occupies the Fe coordination sites, while valence-band X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VB-XPS) confirms enhanced electronic coupling in the Ni–O–In framework. Density functional theory (DFT) additionally suggests that the In 5p orbitals strongly hybridize with the O 2p and Ni 3d states, establishing a Ni3d-O2p-In5p electronic interaction that regulates the Ni electronic structure and optimizes the adsorption energies of O-containing intermediates. The resulting d-p-p orbital hybridization offers an efficient pathway for charge delocalization and strengthens the M–O covalency, thereby accelerating the OER kinetics. This study elucidates the structure–activity relationship and identifies p-block metal-induced orbital hybridization as an effective strategy for developing high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts, offering an alternative to conventional transition-metal modification approaches.
n0d483db6fb87: Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and metal halide hydrate. SSNMR unambiguously reveals both the tert-butylammonium cation and the 18-crown-6 macrocycle as independent rotators─a distinction often ambiguous in such systems. Crucially, by correlating SSNMR-derived dynamics of the crown ether with dielectric relaxation of the coordinated water molecule, we uncover their synchronized rotation across a wide temperature range, mediated by charge-assisted hydrogen bonding. These findings reveal a cooperative multirotor gyroscopic model featuring synchronous rotation of an integrated coaxial crown ether–water–ammonium trio-rotator, accompanied by correlated alkyl reorientation. This synergy validates the dielectric relaxation principle in a complex, multirotor crystalline environment where unambiguous peak assignment has been a longstanding challenge. This work establishes a generalizable methodology for dissecting complex, multicomponent dynamics in crystalline materials, directly bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopic dielectric response.
na56b4f9a5963: Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.
n4cfeed1052ca: Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.
n815edb2d6801: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.
nba601eabbaba: Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability (>230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.
n6f11caf20cab: Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance. Using curvature-engineered M–N–C single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we demonstrate that curvature-induced electric fields modulate electron occupation at active sites and shift the potential of zero charge in a controllable manner. This field-driven electronic perturbation selectively tunes adsorbate binding energetics, thereby dictating limiting potentials, steering reaction pathways, and governing the thermodynamics and kinetics of interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer in nitrogen electroreduction. Notably, we uncover an inverted volcano–type dependence of catalytic activity on curvature, wherein optimal activity is achieved within a moderate field-strength window. This nonmonotonic trend underscores the necessity of balanced curvature regulation, rather than simply maximizing field intensity, in optimizing electrocatalytic performance. These findings provide a quantitative framework for monitoring and regulating catalytic trends under realistic operating conditions via curvature-induced electric fields, offering generalizable design principles for diverse SAC systems and electrochemical reactions.
nf961ffd71938: Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.
n39175cb0e5a6: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.
n750648f5ba39: Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.
na500abd96e0f: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.
n63eaef75d86b: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.
nc27262397bb8: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.
naac43e0c5160: The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. However, the low and heterogeneous expression of these receptors often results in suboptimal targeting efficiency. Here, we present an oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle for GA targeting by exploiting sphingomyelin, an abundant component of the GA membrane. This nanoparticle consisted of a polymeric nanocarrier complexed with a plasmid encoding the secreting peptide-deleted α-hemolysin (αHL), a pore-forming protein with high affinity for sphingomyelin. The nanoparticle could transfect cancer cells to induce intracellular expression of αHL, enabling GA targeting through binding to GA-associated sphingomyelin while bypassing the cell membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Intratumoral administration of this formulation significantly suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth and elicited robust antitumor immunity, preventing tumor rechallenge. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.
n7bfd6f158d6b: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.
n0d90144a2e8c: PbZrO3${\rm PbZrO}_3$ is a prototypical antiferroelectric which can be transformed into a ferroelectric under an applied electric field. The abrupt changes in net polarization and spontaneous strain could potentially be utilized for applications in energy storage and microelectromechanical systems. Here, we establish a thermodynamic model that simultaneously incorporates ferroelectric, antiferroelectric, and antiferrodistortive orders. We parameterize it using a combination of experimentally measured lattice parameters, critical transition fields, and dielectric constants as well as first‐principles calculations of electric polarization and crystallographic analysis. We obtain a Clapeyron‐like equation for describing the temperature dependence of critical electric fields for the antiferroelectric‐ferroelectric phase transition, and their dependence on crystallographic directions. We then calculate the phase‐transition‐induced polarization jump and electromechanical responses of PbZrO3${\rm PbZrO}_3$. Finally, we discuss how to include the phase transition between the ferroelectric R3m$R3m$ and R3c$R3c$ phases in our model. Our model can be employed to predict the ferroelectric and electromechanical responses of PbZrO3${\rm PbZrO}_3$ and implemented in the phase‐field method to simulate the mesoscale domain evolution of PbZrO3${\rm PbZrO}_3$ under different thermodynamic conditions.
nd4cb31036652: HfO2‐based ferroelectrics are essential for the next generation of CMOS‐compatible memory and logic devices, yet their performance is governed by a complex interplay between oxygen vacancies, dopants, and structural defects that remains an active area of investigation. These defects shape the function‐critical dynamic phenomena, such as polar phase stabilization, wake‐up, fatigue, and imprint. In this Perspective, we review the limitations of established high‐resolution structural characterization techniques and propose atom probe tomography (APT) as a powerful tool for the 3D atomic‐scale mapping of all constituent species in hafnia‐based ferroelectric systems. By resolving individual dopants, vacancy clustering, and interfacial segregation, APT can facilitate a quantitative understanding of defect‐property relations in hafnia‐based ferroelectrics. We discuss current experimental challenges for APT application to ferroelectric oxides, demonstrate a proof‐of‐concept of atomic‐scale reconstruction in a hafnia‐based device stack, and highlight the potential of APT to guide the development of ferroelectric structures with enhanced reliability and performance.
n8b4abcabc1a5: The spin cycloid characteristic of noncollinear antiferromagnets offers significant potential for energy‐efficient, magnon‐mediated spintronic applications. Multiferroic BiFeO3 is among the most promising candidate materials because its antiferromagnetic order can be controlled by an electric field. However, in epitaxial BiFeO3 thin films, substrate clamping and epitaxial strain modify the cycloidal magnetic structure while limiting efficient ferroelastic‐ferroelectric switching. Here, we show that strain‐released freestanding BiFeO3 membranes overcome these limitations. Compared with substrate‐clamped epitaxial thin films, a 100‐nm‐thick freestanding membrane exhibits ≈50% faster electric‐field‐driven ferroelectric switching and a spatially uniform, bulk‐like single spin cycloid, as revealed by resonant elastic X‐ray scattering. In contrast, the epitaxial thin film exhibits an expanded cycloid periodicity and slower ferroelectric switching dynamics, reflecting the influence of substrate‐induced strain. Freestanding BiFeO3 membranes therefore overcome substrate‐induced constraints by simultaneously restoring the intrinsic bulk‐like spin cycloid and enabling substantially faster ferroelectric switching. This combination of robust noncollinear antiferromagnetic order and efficient electric‐field switching establishes freestanding BiFeO3 membranes as a promising magnetoelectric platform for low‐power magnonic and spintronic technologies, while enabling heterogeneous integration with Si‐based devices.
n6acef72cb969: Understanding and controlling the chemical states both in the bulk and at the interfaces of complex oxide thin films is essential for engineering a wide range of electronic, optical, and magnetic functionalities, which arise through emergent phenomena such as two‐dimensional electron gases, interfacial magnetism, and associated phase transitions. Here, we demonstrate the use of in situ Auger Electron Spectroscopy (AES) as a powerful tool for probing oxidation states and dynamic chemical processes during the growth of complex oxide heterostructures. By leveraging the chemical sensitivity of AES to subtle changes in valence electron populations, we show that this technique can distinguish distinct oxidation states in multivalent perovskite manganate and vanadate systems with high fidelity during deposition. Furthermore, we show evidence for dynamic chemical phenomena, specifically charge transfer processes at the polar–nonpolar LaMnO3${\rm LaMnO}_3$/SrTiO3${\rm SrTiO}_3$ interface. Our results establish in situ AES as a powerful diagnostic tool for monitoring and controlling interfacial chemistry during thin film growth, offering a pathway toward the atomic‐scale engineering of chemical states in functional oxide heterostructures.
na7a6597f4954: In BiFeO3 thin films, the interplay of interfacial chemistry, electrostatics, and epitaxial strain is engineered to stabilize homohelicity in polarization textures at the domain scale. The synergistic use of a Bi2O2‐terminated Aurivillius buffer layer and a highly anisotropic compressive epitaxial strain offers new routes to control the polar‐texture helicity in oxide ferroelectrics, enabling functional domain‐wall and domain‐based electronics. Abstract The balance between interfacial chemistry, electrostatics, and epitaxial strain plays a crucial role in stabilizing polarization in ferroelectric thin films. Here, these contributions are brought into competition in BiFeO3 (BFO) thin films grown on the charged‐surface‐terminated La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 (LSMO)‐buffered NdGaO3 (001) substrates. The large anisotropic compressive strain from the substrate promotes the formation of ferroelectric domains despite the expected stabilization of a uniform out‐of‐plane polarization by the (La,Sr)O0.7+ termination of the metallic buffer. Piezoresponse force microscopy and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal that the resulting nanoscale domain architecture is stabilized by the deterministic formation of a fluorite‐like Bi2O2 surface layer on regions polarized oppositely to the LSMO‐imposed polarization orientation. Leveraging this polarization compensation mechanism, a uniform out‐of‐plane polarization is stabilized in the highly strained BFO films by inserting a Bi2O2‐terminated Aurivillius film as a buffer layer. Additionally, signatures of homohelicity in polarization textures of the BFO films are revealed on the level of domain configurations using local polarization switching experiments. The work thus brings new strategies for controlling polarization direction and helicity in oxide ferroelectrics, opening pathways for functional domain‐wall and domain‐based electronics.
n569d3386190d: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.
nc0d68a27df2f: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment—marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers—prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood‐spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro‐ and micro‐scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high‐value payloads—including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides—directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.
nc4d220330e95: Remote‐controlled genetic circuits use externally applied physical signals to regulate gene expression and cellular functions with spatial and temporal precision. Light, ultrasound, and magnetic fields provide complementary advantages in controllability, tissue accessibility, and biological compatibility, but their performance depends on both physical‐field propagation and efficient conversion of external energy into intracellular signals and predictable gene‐regulatory outputs. This review presents a unified framework of physical transduction, biological sensors, signal processors, and genetic effectors for comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Core genetic circuits are distinguished from delivery and auxiliary platforms that support cargo release, cellular uptake, or energy conversion without directly regulating genes. Representative systems are compared by circuit architecture, transduction mechanism, stimulus parameters, dynamic range, basal leakage, response kinetics, reversibility, in vivo actuation, delivery requirements, and safety. The evolution from inducible switches toward multi‐input logic, tunable regulation, genetic memory, and feedback control is discussed. An end‐to‐end codesign workflow and modality‐specific reporting framework are proposed to integrate physical inputs, transducers, genetic circuits, delivery strategies, and stimulation devices. Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.
n7a53db902120: Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet‐based microfluidic platform for the high‐throughput generation of morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel (2NT‐GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical‐sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT‐GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.
nc948c616cdd0: Developing highly stable, low‐iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co‐doped manganese‐cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La‐MCOδ, featuring octahedral La–Ir pairs (Laoct–Iroct) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z‐axis oxygen vacancies. This low‐Ir catalyst Ir,La‐MCOδ (0.12 mg Ir cm−2) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm−2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton–electron transfer pathway. This mechanism preserves the structural integrity of the catalyst and yields a calculated reaction free‐energy change of merely 0.38 eV (U = 1.23 V) for the most unfavorable oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling elementary step, thereby endowing Ir,La‐MCOδ with exceptional durability. This work provides a valuable mechanistic insight into designing highly stable defective catalysts.
n7a930b6016f4: Nanoscale zero‐valent iron (nZVI) is the most promising reductant for in situ groundwater remediation, but its field application around the world is quite limited for decades, due to significant reductivity loss by water oxidation during long‐term (e.g., years) application. Herein, we report a polysiloxane(Fe)‐modified nZVI (PSO(Fe)‐nZVI, 269.0 ± 23.5 nm) featuring loosened hydrophobic C16 chains and Si─O groups on the surface and interior. Remarkably, after 420‐day aging in water, PSO(Fe)‐nZVI exhibits 102‐fold and 211‐fold enhancements of reduction rate constants for trichloroethylene and Cr(VI), respectively, 4‐order‐of‐magnitude higher than nZVI. The loosened C16 chains on PSO(Fe)‐nZVI could regulate Fe(0)→Fe(II) reaction in water to enhance specific surface area by 131 folds and expose more active Fe species. The Si─O groups could combine with Fe(II) and inhibit the Fe(II)→Fe(III) reaction to reserve 70.8% of active Fe species. This work highlights the regulation of corrosion reactions by surface engineering to boost the reduction performance of nZVI for long‐term groundwater remediation.
n7cb08170a2d7: Fluoride‐ion batteries (FIBs) are appealing for their high theoretical energy density and low cost, wherein aqueous electrolytes provide the exceptionally high fluoride‐salt solubility and fast ion transport. However, the strong H2O−H2O hydrogen‐bond network promotes the proton/hydroxide shuttling and leaves the reactive free water at interface, leading to parasitic reactions, corrosion and active‐material dissolution, which severely limit cycling stability. Here we show that reconfiguring the hydrogen‐bond network of water offers a molecular‐level pathway to stabilize aqueous FIB chemistry. We report a bioinspired hydrogel electrolyte by introducing hyaluronic acid (HA) into CsF aqueous electrolyte, together with ethylene glycol (EG) as an antifreezing co‐solvent. HA reorganizes the hydrogen‐bond network to immobilize free water and suppress water activity, while HA/EG jointly regulate the solvation environment of F−, reducing the hydration level and facilitating the interfacial fluoride transfer. The HA‐based electrolyte forms a robust, chemically rich CEI containing organic (O/N‐containing) and fluoride‐rich inorganic components, which mitigates interfacial side reactions and suppresses active species dissolution. A CuF2||Pb full cell delivers the stable cycling with a ∼0.5 V discharge plateau and retains over 100 mAh·g−1 after 160 cycles, and further demonstrates the reversible FIB operation down to −20°C for the first time.
n014a8b48740f: Cyanogramide (1) is a unique spirooxindole alkaloid derived from a marine actinomycete and is characterized by its distinct spirocyclic pyrrolo[1,2‐c]imidazolidin‐4‐one scaffold. Although we have successfully elucidated the biosynthetic pathway of 1, the mechanism underlying the formation of the characteristic imidazolidin‐4‐one remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase CyaI catalyzes an oxidation reaction through a zwitterionic intermediate and facilitates a subsequent unusual C→N acetyl migration, which triggers a spontaneous intramolecular cyclization to forge the imidazolidin‐4‐one ring during 1 biosynthesis. In addition, CyaI is identified as a bifunctional enzyme that also catalyzes N‐demethylation. High‐resolution crystallography and mutagenesis studies determine Thr245 as a crucial catalytic residue that modulates the balance between imidazolidine‐4‐one synthesis and demethylation. This work not only expands the catalytic repertoire of P450 enzymes but also opens the way for the development of multifunctional biocatalysts in the synthesis of complex natural products.
n978821ea48e9: High-voltage sodium metal batteries (SMBs) suffer from fast degradation stemming from the interfacial incompatibility between electrolytes and electrodes. In this study, potassium 3-pyridyltrifluoroborate (KPBF3) is proposed as a dual-interface electrolyte additive, where the pyridine moiety can effectively modulate the anion's electronic structure, lowering its lowest unoccupied molecular orbital energy level and enhancing its binding affinity for Na+. This promotes the preferential reductive decomposition of PBF3 −, forming a robust NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase that suppresses Na dendrite growth. Simultaneously, the cleavage of B─F bonds facilitates the formation of a thin and uniform NaF-rich cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), significantly suppressing electrolyte oxidation and greatly improving the high-voltage stability. Consequently, Na||Na symmetric cells achieve an ultra-long cycling life of 6000 h at 5 mA cm−2, while Na||Cu cells exhibit a high average Coulombic efficiency (ACE) of 99.89%. Moreover, Na||Na3V2(PO4)2F3 cells demonstrate 90.8% capacity retention over 10000 cycles at 10 C and 4.3 V, and 90.0% retention after 2500 cycles at 4.4 V. Notably, this additive also enables SMBs with a low N/P ratio of 2.65 to deliver a high capacity retention of 88.4% after 1000 cycles.
n52f16a06ff68: Photocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (PNitRR) offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis and wastewater treatment. The insufficient utilization of near-infrared (NIR) light and sluggish reaction kinetics of coupled water oxidation result in unsatisfactory performance. Herein, a conductive metal organic framework (cMOF)-on-cMOF S-scheme heterojunction is reported as an efficient full-spectrum photocatalyst for driving an innovative hybrid system of PNitRR to NH3 and photocatalytic 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction (PHMFOR) to 2, 5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA). The integration of Co-cMOF and Ni-cMOF with dual NIR-response features and well-matched band structures into an S-scheme heterojunction enables sufficient light utilization and efficient charge separation. Moreover, the formation of interfacial Ni-Co dual sites with modulated electronic structures accounts for PNitRR and PHMFOR, respectively, with enhanced activity and selectivity. The designed cMOF-on-cMOF S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst exhibits production rates of 4677.5 and 5932.5 µmol gcat −1 h−1 with apparent quantum yields of 13.3% and 13.1% at 500 nm for NH3 and FDCA production, respectively. This work opens new avenues for the development of advanced photocatalysts and integrated photocatalytic systems to produce valuable chemicals.
n8a83be241350: Ultrasensitive detection of nonpolar toxic VOCs like toluene remains a great challenge for environmental monitoring. This work presents a rationally designed SERS platform based on metallized covalent organic frameworks (M‐COFs, M = Fe, Ni, Cu) obtained by a mild metal‐modulation strategy that enables metal‑tunable COF crystallinity and porosity. M‐COFs were one‐pot synthesized from PyTA and PDA under 70 °C and atmospheric pressure. Spectroscopic characterizations confirm atomic dispersion of M2+ with four‐coordinate M─N/O bonding in the frameworks. Particularly, Fe─COF exhibits superior crystallinity and an enhanced BET surface area of 2078 m2 g−1 with a pore size of 1.87 nm, whereas Ni‑ and Cu─COF show reduced structural order. The Au/Fe─COF SERS platform achieves a toluene detection limit of 0.1 ppb with an enhancement factor of 1.5 × 106, outperforming Ni─COF (0.5 ppb), Cu─COF (1 ppm), and metal‐free COF (10 ppb). DFT calculations verify Fe─COF ’s ultrahigh toluene adsorption affinity with an adsorption energy of −34.17 kcal mol−1 and its higher crystallinity compared to its counterparts. This platform also shows excellent anti‐interference and enables specific toluene detection in complex gas mixtures. The M‐COF‐based SERS system offers a practical solution for ultra‐trace nonpolar VOC monitoring.
nd0573c78752c: Organic short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) imaging is a promising technology for consumer electronics and a broad range of other applications. The bottleneck of organic SWIR imaging is the lack of electron acceptors with ultrasmall bandgaps. Herein, we develop ultrasmall‐bandgap electron acceptors by cyclizing the exocyclic vinylene linkers of a typical acceptor–donor–acceptor (A–D–A) electron acceptor with tetrafluorobenzene moieties. This tetrafluorobenzene cyclization redshifts the absorption spectrum by 224 nm and reduces the trap density of states of the neat film by nearly one order of magnitude. The resulting organic photodetector exhibits a peak responsivity of 0.36 A W−1, a noise current of 1.41 × 10−11 A Hz−1/2 at 1 kHz, a specific detectivity exceeding 109 Jones at 1140 nm under −1 V bias, and a linear dynamic range of 82 dB. Monolithic integration of this organic photodetector with thin‐film transistor arrays yields a 256 × 256 pixel imager capable of high‐contrast SWIR imaging. This work establishes tetrafluorobenzene cyclization as a powerful molecular paradigm for ultrasmall bandgap organic semiconductors, paving the way for low‐cost, heavy‐metal‐free SWIR imagers in consumer electronics.
ncdc1b02a13c3: Synthetic ion channels with efficient ion transport activity can disrupt the ion homeostasis of cancer cells and exhibit potential for tumor therapy. Herein, a helix‐based ion channel was constructed via a one‐pot synthesis strategy. This channel is composed of two interconnected proton channel (quinoline helix) and chloride ion channel (aligned thiourea moieties), which is named as “dual ion channel.” This dual ion channel can insert into the phospholipid membrane through a single‐molecule form and flux H+ and Cl− across the membrane simultaneously. Interestingly, this dual ion channel also exhibits “ON‐OFF” switchable ion transport behaviors in response to external temperature variation. Under physiological environment (37°C), this channel achieves highly efficient ion transport and reveals remarkable anticancer activity against U87 cells with an IC50 value of 0.14 µM, which is comparable to commercial chemotherapy drugs.
